title.zh: 卷二百六十三 列傳第二十二 張昭 竇儀 呂餘慶 劉熙古 石熙載 李穆
title.en: Volume 263 Biographies 22: Zhang Zhao, Dou Yi, Lu Yuqing, Liu Xigu, Shi Xizai, Li Mu
title.raw: 卷二百六十三 列傳第二十二 張昭 竇儀 呂餘慶 劉熙古 石熙載 李穆 Volume 263 Biographies 22: Zhang Zhao, Dou Yi, Lu Yuqing, Liu Xigu, Shi Xizai, Li Mu

sentences.zh: 張昭，字潛夫，本名昭遠，避漢祖諱，止稱昭。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao, style Qianfu, original personal name Zhaoyuan; to avoid the taboo of the Han founder, he used only the name Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Qianfu, was originally named Zhaoyuan; to avoid the taboo name of the Han founder, he went by Zhao alone.

sentences.zh: 自言漢常山王耳之後，世居濮州范縣。

translations.literal: He said himself to be a descendant of Prince Er of Changshan of Han, and his family for generations resided in Fan County, Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Liu Er, Prince of Changshan under the Han, and said his family had long lived in Fan County in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖楚平，壽張令。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Chu Ping, magistrate of Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chu Ping had served as magistrate of Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 楚平生直，即昭父也。

translations.literal: Chu Ping had a son named Zhi, who was Zhao's father.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Ping's son was named Zhi—Zhao's father.

sentences.zh: 初，楚平赴調長安，值巢寇亂，不知所終。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chu Ping went to Chang'an on assignment for an official post; he encountered Huang Chao's rebellion and his end was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chu Ping had traveled to Chang'an for an official appointment when Huang Chao's rebels rose; nothing was ever heard of him again.

sentences.zh: 直幼避地河朔，既冠，以父失所在，時盜賊蠭起，道路榛梗，乃自秦抵蜀，徒行丐食，求父所在，積十年不能得。

translations.literal: Zhi in youth fled to refuge north of the Yellow River; after reaching manhood, because his father's whereabouts were unknown and bandits swarmed while roads were choked with brush, he went from Qin to Shu on foot, begging food, seeking his father's location—for ten years he could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhi fled the turmoil to the north of the Yellow River. After he came of age, with his father still missing and bandits everywhere choking the roads, he walked from Qin into Shu, begging as he went to find him—and after ten years still could not.

sentences.zh: 乃發哀行服，躬耕海濱。

translations.literal: Thereupon he put on mourning and performed the rites, and himself plowed by the seashore.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered mourning and farmed with his own hands on the coast.

sentences.zh: 青州王師範開學館，延置儒士，再以書幣招直，署賓職。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan of Qingzhou opened a school hall, invited and placed Confucian scholars, and twice with letters and gifts recruited Zhi, appointing him to a guest post.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan of Qingzhou founded an academy and gathered scholars; twice he sent letters and gifts to win Zhi over and gave him a post as a guest officer.

sentences.zh: 師範降梁，直脫難北歸，以《周易》、《春秋》教授，學者自遠而至，時號「逍遙先生」。

translations.literal: When Shifan surrendered to Liang, Zhi escaped hardship and returned north, teaching the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals; scholars came from afar, and at the time he was called "Master Free-and-Easy."
translations.idiomatic: When Shifan submitted to Liang, Zhi made his way north out of danger and taught the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals; students came from far away, and people called him "Master Free-and-Easy."

sentences.zh: 昭始十歲，能誦古樂府、詠史詩百餘篇；

translations.literal: Zhao at the beginning was ten years old and could recite more than a hundred ancient Music Bureau poems and historical ballads;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was only ten when he could recite more than a hundred old yuefu pieces and historical poems;

sentences.zh: 未冠，遍讀《九經》，盡通其義。

translations.literal: Before the capping ceremony, he read through the Nine Classics and fully understood their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he had read all the Nine Classics and mastered their meaning.

sentences.zh: 處儕類中，緩步闊視，以為馬、鄭不己若也。

translations.literal: Among his peers he walked slowly with a broad gaze, thinking that even Ma and Zheng were not his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Among his peers he walked slowly with a sweeping look, convinced that not even Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan were his match.

sentences.zh: 後至贊皇，遇程生者，專史學，以為專究經旨，不通今古，率多拘滯，繁而寡要；

translations.literal: Later he reached Zanhuang and met a Mr. Cheng who specialized in historical studies; Zhao held that those who devoted themselves only to the classics' purport did not connect past and present, were mostly rigid and obstructive, prolix yet lacking essentials;
translations.idiomatic: Later at Zanhuang he met a Mr. Cheng who specialized in history. Zhao argued that scholars who buried themselves in the classics' letter knew past and present poorly—mostly rigid, wordy, and thin on what mattered;

sentences.zh: 若極談王霸，經緯治亂，非史不可。

translations.literal: but to discuss fully kingship and hegemony and to weave together order and disorder, history was indispensable.
translations.idiomatic: but to speak fully of kingship and hegemony and to thread order and chaos together, one could not do without history.

sentences.zh: 因出班、范《漢書》十餘義商榷，乃授昭《荀紀》、《國志》等，後又盡得十三史，五七年間，能馳騁上下數千百年事。

translations.literal: He therefore brought out more than ten points from Ban and Fan's Book of Han for discussion; Cheng then gave Zhao the Han Records by Xun and the Records of the Three Kingdoms and the like; later Zhao obtained all of the Thirteen Histories, and within five or seven years could range freely over events spanning thousands of years.
translations.idiomatic: He raised more than ten points from Ban Gu and Fan Ye's Book of Han for debate; Cheng then lent him Xun Yue's Han Records, Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, and the rest. Within five or seven years Zhao had mastered all thirteen standard histories and could move freely across thousands of years of events.

sentences.zh: 又注《十代興亡論》。

translations.literal: He also annotated the Treatise on the Rise and Fall of Ten Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a commentary on the Treatise on the Rise and Fall of Ten Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 處亂世，躬耕負米以養親。

translations.literal: Living in a chaotic age, he himself plowed and carried rice on his back to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In those troubled times he farmed himself and carried rice on his back to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 後唐莊宗入魏，河朔遊士，多自效軍門，昭因至魏，攜文數十軸謁興唐尹張憲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang entered Wei, wandering scholars of Hebei mostly offered themselves to military gates; Zhao accordingly went to Wei, carrying several dozen scrolls of writings to call on Zhang Xian, prefect of Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, many wandering scholars from north of the Yellow River sought posts in the armies. Zhao went to Wei as well, carrying several dozen scrolls of his writing to visit Zhang Xian, prefect of Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 憲家富文籍，每與昭燕語，講論經史要事，恨相見之晚，即署府推官。

translations.literal: Xian's household was rich in books; whenever he conversed leisurely with Zhao and discussed essentials of the classics and histories, he regretted their late meeting and immediately appointed him push officer of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's household was rich in books. In their easy conversations on weighty matters of the classics and histories he lamented they had met so late and at once appointed Zhao push officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 同光初，奏授真秩，加監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, he was memorialized for a regular rank and additionally made acting supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongguang era he was memorialized for a regular rank and made an acting supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 憲為北京留守，昭亦從至晉陽。

translations.literal: When Xian became governor of the Northern Capital, Zhao also followed him to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian became governor of the Northern Capital, Zhao followed him to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗及難，聞鄴中兵士推戴明宗，憲部將符彥超合戍將應之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong met calamity, word came that soldiers in Ye had elevated Mingzong; Xian's subordinate general Fu Yanchao joined the garrison commanders in responding.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong fell into crisis, word came that the troops at Ye had raised Mingzong. Xian's subordinate Fu Yanchao rallied the garrison commanders to join them.

sentences.zh: 昭謂憲曰：「得無奉表勸進為自安之計乎？」

translations.literal: Zhao said to Xian: "Would it not be well to submit a memorial urging enthronement as a plan for your own security?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said to Xian, "Might you not submit a memorial urging enthronement—as a way to secure yourself?"

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「我本書生，見知主上，位至保𨤲，乃布衣之極。

translations.literal: Xian said: "I was originally a plain scholar, noticed and trusted by our lord, and rose to Grand Chancellor—the utmost for one in coarse cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "I was only a scholar when our lord noticed and trusted me; I rose to Grand Chancellor—the highest a commoner could reach.

sentences.zh: 苟靦顏求生，何面目見主於地下？」

translations.literal: If I shamelessly seek to live on, with what face could I meet our lord in the grave?"
translations.idiomatic: If I shame my face to cling to life, how could I face our lord in the grave?"

sentences.zh: 昭曰：「此古人之志也，公能行之，死且不朽矣。」

translations.literal: Zhao said: "This is the will of the ancients; if you can act on it, even in death you will be imperishable."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "That is the resolve of the ancients. If you can do it, your death will be deathless."

sentences.zh: 相泣而去，憲遂死之，時論重昭能成憲之節。

translations.literal: They wept and parted; Xian thereupon died for his integrity, and public opinion valued Zhao for helping Xian fulfill his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and parted. Xian died for his lord, and contemporaries praised Zhao for helping him keep his integrity.

sentences.zh: 時有害昭者，昭曰：「明誠所至，期不再生，主辱臣亡，死而無悔。」

translations.literal: At the time there were those who wished to harm Zhao; Zhao said: "Where sincerity reaches, one does not expect to live again; when the lord is shamed the minister dies—death without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Some then wanted Zhao killed. He said, "Where sincerity goes, one does not expect to live again. When the lord is shamed the minister dies—and I die without regret."

sentences.zh: 眾執以送彥超，彥超曰：「推官正人，無得害之。」

translations.literal: The crowd seized him and brought him to Yanchao; Yanchao said: "The push officer is a righteous man—he must not be harmed."
translations.idiomatic: The mob seized him and brought him to Yanchao, who said, "The push officer is an upright man. Do not harm him."

sentences.zh: 又逼昭為榜安撫軍民。

translations.literal: They also compelled Zhao to draft a placard to reassure the army and the people.
translations.idiomatic: They also forced Zhao to draft a proclamation to reassure the troops and the people.

sentences.zh: 事寧，以昭為北京留守推官，加殿中侍御史、內供奉官，賜緋。

translations.literal: When things settled, Zhao was made push officer to the Northern Capital governor, with additional offices as attendant censor within the palace and inner palace attendant, and was granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, Zhao was made push officer to the Northern Capital governor, with additional posts as palace attendant censor and inner attendant, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 天成三年，改安義軍節度掌書記。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng, he was transferred to secretary under the Anyi military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng he was transferred to secretary under the Anyi military commission.

sentences.zh: 時以武皇、莊宗實錄未修，詔正國軍節度盧質、西川節度副使何瓚、秘書監韓彥輝纘錄事跡。

translations.literal: At the time, because the Veritable Records of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong had not yet been compiled, the court ordered Lu Zhi, military commissioner of Zhenguo, He Zan, vice commissioner of the Xichuan military commission, and Han Yanhui, director of the Secretariat, to gather and record their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Veritable Records of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong had not yet been written, the court ordered Lu Zhi, commissioner of Zhenguo, He Zan, vice commissioner of Xichuan, and Han Yanhui, director of the Secretariat, to collect and record their deeds.

sentences.zh: 瓚上言：「昭有史材，嘗私撰《同光實錄》十二卷，又聞其欲撰三祖志，並藏昭宗朝賜武皇制詔九十餘篇，請以昭所撰送史館。」

translations.literal: Zan submitted: "Zhao has talent for history; he once privately compiled twelve juan of Veritable Records of the Tongguang reign, and it is also heard that he intends to compile a chronicle of the three ancestors, and moreover preserves more than ninety edicts and commands given by Emperor Zhaozong to the Martial Emperor—please send what Zhao has written to the History Office."
translations.idiomatic: Zan memorialized: "Zhao has a historian's gifts. He has privately compiled twelve juan of Veritable Records of the Tongguang reign, intends a chronicle of the three ancestors, and keeps more than ninety edicts Emperor Zhaozong issued to the Martial Emperor. Please send his writings to the History Office."

sentences.zh: 拜昭為左補闕、史館修撰，委之撰錄。

translations.literal: Zhao was appointed Left Remonstrator and History Office compiler, with the task of compilation entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was appointed Left Remonstrator and History Office compiler and entrusted with the compilation.

sentences.zh: 昭以懿祖、獻祖、太祖並不踐帝位，仍補為《紀年錄》二十卷，又撰《莊宗實錄》三十卷上之。

translations.literal: Because the August, Exalted, and Martial ancestors had never ascended the throne, Zhao nevertheless supplemented a Chronicle in twenty juan, and also compiled thirty juan of Veritable Records of Zhuangzong and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the August, Exalted, and Martial ancestors had never actually reigned, Zhao still compiled a twenty-juan Chronicle and submitted thirty juan of Veritable Records of Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒美，遷都官員外郎。

translations.literal: An excellent edict praised him, and he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued a commendatory edict and promoted him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時皇子競尚奢侈，昭疏諫曰：

translations.literal: At the time princes competed in luxury; Zhao submitted a remonstrance saying:
translations.idiomatic: Princes were then vying in extravagance. Zhao submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 「帝王之子，長於深宮，安於逸樂，紛華之玩，絲竹之音，日接於耳目，不與驕期而驕自至。

translations.literal: " Sons of emperors, reared in deep palaces and settled in ease and pleasure, with gaudy playthings and the sounds of strings and pipes daily reaching their eyes and ears—without appointing a time for pride, pride arrives of itself.
translations.idiomatic: " A son of an emperor grows up deep in the palace, at ease in pleasure. Ornament and music meet his eyes and ears every day; pride needs no appointment—it comes on its own.

sentences.zh: 儻非天資英敏，識本清明，以此蕩心，焉能無惑。

translations.literal: Unless by nature he is keen and bright and his understanding fundamentally clear, with such things unsettling the mind, how could he be without confusion?
translations.idiomatic: Unless he is gifted and clear-minded by nature, how can such things unsettle his heart and leave him unconfused?

sentences.zh: 苟不豫為教道，何以置之盤牙？

translations.literal: If one does not beforehand provide instruction, how can one place him in the heir's position?
translations.idiomatic: If you do not teach him beforehand, how can you set him in the heir's place?

sentences.zh: 臣見先帝時，皇子、皇弟盡喜無稽玩物之言，厭聞致治經邦之論，入則務飾姬姜，出則廣增僕馬；

translations.literal: Your subject has seen that under the late emperor, imperial sons and younger imperial brothers all delighted in frivolous talk of playthings and disliked hearing discourse on bringing order and governing the realm; within they busied themselves adorning concubines, without they widely increased servants and horses;
translations.idiomatic: I saw under the late emperor that princes and younger imperial brothers loved idle talk of trifles and hated counsel on governing the realm. Indoors they dressed their women; outdoors they multiplied servants and horses;

sentences.zh: 親賓滿坐，食客盈門，箴規者少，諧謔者多。

translations.literal: kinsmen and guests filled the seats, retainers crowded the gates—few admonished, many jested.
translations.idiomatic: kinsmen and guests filled the hall, hangers-on packed the gate—few who admonished, many who jested.

sentences.zh: 以此而欲託以主鬯，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: With this, to wish to entrust to him the chief sacrifice—is it not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: To entrust the ancestral rites to such men—is that not hard?

sentences.zh: 臣請諸皇子各置師傅，陛下令皇子屈身師事之，講論道德。

translations.literal: Your subject asks that each prince be given a tutor; may Your Majesty order the princes to humble themselves and serve them as teachers, discussing moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each prince be given a tutor and that Your Majesty make them humble themselves to study under them and discuss moral principle.

sentences.zh: 使一日之中，止記一事，一歲之內，所記漸多。

translations.literal: Let them in one day record only one matter; within one year what is recorded will gradually increase.
translations.idiomatic: Have them record only one thing each day; over a year what they have recorded will grow.

sentences.zh: 每月終，令師傅具錄聞奏。

translations.literal: At each month's end, have the tutors compile the records and report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end let the tutors compile the records and report them.

sentences.zh: 或皇子上謁之時，陛下更令侍臣面問，十中得五，為益良多，博識安危之理，深知成敗之由。

translations.literal: Or when princes attend audience, may Your Majesty further have attendant ministers question them face to face; if five of ten are answered, the benefit will be great—they will broadly know the principles of safety and peril and deeply understand the causes of success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Or when a prince attends audience, let attendant ministers question him in person. If he answers half the questions, the gain will be great: he will know why states stand or fall and understand success and failure at its roots.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞古之人君，即位而封太子、拜諸王，究其所由，蓋有深旨。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that in antiquity, when a ruler took the throne he enfeoffed the crown prince and invested the imperial princes; examining the reason, there was surely deep purpose in it.
translations.idiomatic: I have also read that in antiquity, when a ruler took the throne he enfeoffed the crown prince and invested the imperial princes, and there was deep purpose in this.

sentences.zh: 使庶不亂嫡，疏不間親，禮秩有常，邪慝不作。

translations.literal: It kept younger sons from overturning the heir, kept the distant from coming between the close, kept ritual ranks constant, and kept wickedness from arising.
translations.idiomatic: It kept younger sons from overturning the heir, kept the distant from coming between kin, kept ritual ranks constant, and kept wickedness from arising.

sentences.zh: 近代人君，失於此道，以至邦家構患，釁隙萌生。

translations.literal: Rulers of recent times have failed in this way, until states and families bred calamity and rifts began to sprout.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers of recent times have lost this way, until states and families bred calamity and rifts began to grow.

sentences.zh: 昔隋祖聰明，煬帝亦傾楊勇；

translations.literal: In the past the Sui founder was wise, yet Emperor Yang also toppled Yang Yong;
translations.idiomatic: In the past the Sui founder was wise, yet Emperor Yang also toppled Yang Yong;

sentences.zh: 太宗齊聖，魏王終覆承乾。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang was sagely in full measure, yet the Prince of Wei finally overthrew Chengqian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang was wholly sagely, yet the Prince of Wei finally overthrew Chengqian.

sentences.zh: 臣每讀古書，深悲其事。

translations.literal: Whenever your subject reads the ancient books, he deeply grieves these affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the ancient books, I deeply grieve these affairs.

sentences.zh: 願於聖代，杜此厲階。

translations.literal: May it be that in this sagely age this source of ruin is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: May this sagely age block this source of ruin.

sentences.zh: 其於卜貳封宗，在臣未敢輕議。

translations.literal: As for choosing the heir and enfeoffing the imperial clan, your subject does not dare speak lightly.
translations.idiomatic: As for choosing the heir and enfeoffing the imperial clan, I do not dare speak lightly.

sentences.zh: 臣請諸皇子於恩澤賜與之間，婚姻省侍之際，依嫡庶而為禮秩，據親疏而定節文，示以等威，絕其徼幸，保宗之道，莫大於斯。」

translations.literal: Your subject asks that among the imperial princes, in the granting of favors and gifts and in marriage and attendance at court, ritual rank be set according to legitimacy and birth order and ceremonial forms be fixed according to closeness and distance, showing equal majesty and cutting off grasping hope—the way to preserve the imperial house has nothing greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that among the imperial princes, in the granting of favors and in marriage and attendance at court, ritual rank follow legitimacy and birth order and ceremonial forms follow closeness and distance, showing equal majesty and cutting off grasping hope—nothing is greater than this for preserving the imperial house."

sentences.zh: 明宗覽疏而不用。

translations.literal: Mingzong read the memorial but did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong read the memorial but did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 四年，上《武王以來功臣列傳》三十卷，以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he submitted thirty juan of Biographies of Meritorious Officials from King Wu onward, and with his existing office was made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he submitted thirty juan of Biographies of Meritorious Officials from King Wu of Zhou onward and was made drafter of edicts in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 明宗好畋獵，昭疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Mingzong loved hunting; Zhao submitted a remonstrance saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong loved the hunt. Zhao submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 「太祖初鎮太原，每年打鹿於北鄙；

translations.literal: " When the Martial Ancestor first governed Taiyuan, each year he hunted deer on the northern frontier;
translations.idiomatic: " When the Martial Ancestor first held Taiyuan, he hunted deer on the northern marches each year;

sentences.zh: 先帝在位，暇日射鴈於近郊。

translations.literal: when the late emperor was on the throne, on leisure days he shot geese in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: when the late emperor reigned, he shot geese near the capital on his free days.

sentences.zh: 此蓋軍務之餘，畋遊自適。

translations.literal: This was merely amid military affairs, hunting for one's own ease.
translations.idiomatic: That was sport after military business—a hunt for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 洎先帝因圖啟祚，嚮明御宇，則宜易彼諸侯之事，肅乎萬乘之儀。

translations.literal: When the late emperor by design opened the succession and turned toward enlightened rule of the realm, he ought to have changed those feudal-lord matters and made solemn the rites of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Once the late emperor took the throne by design and turned to enlightened rule, he should have left feudal habits behind and kept the dignity due the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 而猶因習舊風，失其威重，驅逐原獸，殆無虛日。

translations.literal: Yet he still followed old custom, lost his august weight, and drove wild beasts—almost no day was idle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept the old ways, lost his majesty, and chased game in the wild—hardly a day without it.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為事有可畏者四焉。

translations.literal: Your subject in his foolishness holds that there are four matters to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject believes there are four things to fear.

sentences.zh: 洛都舊制，宮城與禁苑相連，人君宴遊，不離苑囿，御馬來往，輦路坦夷，不涉荒郊，何憂蹶失。

translations.literal: The old regulation of the Luo capital joined the palace city and the forbidden park; the ruler's feasting and roaming did not leave the park; imperial horses came and went on level carriage roads, not crossing wild suburbs—what worry of stumbling?
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Luoyang practice the palace and the imperial park were joined. The ruler's outings never left the park; imperial horses used level roads and never crossed wild country—what fear of a fall?

sentences.zh: 今則驅馳驂服，涉歷榛蕪，此後節氣嚴凝，徑途凍滑，萬一有銜橛之變，陛下縱自輕，奈宗廟社稷何？

translations.literal: Now you gallop paired teams and cross through brush and weeds; hereafter when the season turns severe and paths freeze slippery, if by any chance there is a bit-bar mishap, even if Your Majesty lightly regards yourself, what of the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain?
translations.idiomatic: Now you gallop paired teams through brush and waste. When the cold sets in and paths ice over, if the bit should fail—even if Your Majesty thinks little of yourself, what of the ancestral temple and the realm?

sentences.zh: 所可畏者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first thing to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first fear.

sentences.zh: 又陛下新有四海，宜以德服萬邦。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has newly possessed the four seas and ought to make the myriad states submit by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty has newly won the realm and should bring the world to submission through virtue.

sentences.zh: 今則江、嶺未平，淮夷尚梗，彼初聞陛下革先朝之失政，還太古之淳風，御物以慈，節財以儉，有典有則，不矜不驕，彼必有三苗率服之心，七旬來格之意。

translations.literal: Now the Yangzi region and the Lingnan are not yet pacified, and the Huai Yi still obstruct; they have just heard that Your Majesty has reformed the previous court's misgovernment, restored the pure winds of high antiquity, governed things with kindness, and economized wealth through frugality, with standards and rules, neither arrogant nor proud—they will surely have the heart of the Three Miao to submit in succession and the intent of the seven-day arrival.
translations.idiomatic: The south of the Yangzi and the Lingnan are not yet settled; the Huai tribes still resist. They have just heard that Your Majesty has corrected the last court's abuses, restored ancient simplicity, ruled with kindness, spent sparingly, kept standards, and shown no arrogance—they will surely feel like the Three Miao ready to submit and like guests coming within seven days.

sentences.zh: 如聞陛下暫遊近甸，彼即以為復好畋遊。

translations.literal: If they hear that Your Majesty makes brief excursions to the near countryside, they will at once think you again love hunting.
translations.idiomatic: If they hear that Your Majesty is hunting again near the capital, they will think the old ways have returned.

sentences.zh: 所可畏者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second thing to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second fear.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞『作法於涼，其弊猶貪，作法於貪，弊將如何？』

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard: 'If one makes law in a cool land, its abuse is still greed; if one makes law in greed, what will the abuse be?'
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard: 'Make law in a cool land and the abuse is still greed; make law in greed—what will the abuse be then?'

sentences.zh: 且打鹿射鴈之事新，敗軌傾輈之轍在，常宜取鑒，不可因循。

translations.literal: Moreover the matters of hunting deer and shooting geese are recent; the tracks of overturned wheels and capsized carriages remain—one should constantly take them as a mirror and must not follow old routine.
translations.idiomatic: Deer hunts and goose shoots are recent; the ruts of overturned wheels are still there. Take them as a warning—do not follow habit.

sentences.zh: 所可畏者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third thing to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third fear.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞『作事可法，貽厥孫謀。』

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard: 'Do deeds that can serve as models—bequeath plans to your descendants.'
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard: 'Do what can be a model—leave plans for your descendants.'

sentences.zh: 若陛下以齊聖廣淵之機，聰明神武之量，其可以宴遊蒐狩之事，少累聖明，所謂『城中好廣眉，城外加半額』，為法之弊，靡不由茲。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty with the capacity of equal sageliness and broad depth and the measure of keen intelligence and divine martial prowess can let feasting, roaming, and hunting slightly burden your sacred clarity—as the saying goes, 'In the city they love broad brows; outside the city they add half a span to the brow'—the abuses of making law never fail to arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's sagely breadth and keen martial gifts, can pleasure outings and the chase burden your clarity even a little? As the proverb says, 'When the city favors broad brows, the suburbs paint half again as wide'—bad laws spread from such examples.

sentences.zh: 所可畏者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth thing to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth fear.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下居高慮遠，慎始圖終，思創業之艱難，知守成之不易，念老氏馳騁之戒，樹文王忠厚之基，約三驅之舊章，定四時之遊幸。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty, dwelling high and considering far, will be careful at the start and plan for the end, reflect on the hardships of founding the enterprise and know the difficulty of preserving what is achieved, remember Laozi's warning against reckless galloping, plant the foundation of King Wen's generous sincerity, restrict yourself to the old rule of the three-sided hunt, and fix seasonal excursions.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty, high above and far-sighted, will be careful at the start and plan for the end, remember how hard it was to found the dynasty and how hard it is to keep it, heed Laozi's warning against reckless riding, lay King Wen's foundation of generous sincerity, keep to the old three-sided hunt, and fix your outings to the seasons.

sentences.zh: 始出有節，後不敢違。」

translations.literal: Let departures at the beginning have measure, and afterward none will dare violate it."
translations.idiomatic: Set limits at the first outing, and later none will dare break them."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，明宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Mingzong praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Mingzong praised it and took his advice.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，丁內艱，賻絹布五十匹，米麥五十石。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing, he mourned his mother; condolence gifts were fifty bolts of silk cloth and fifty piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing he mourned his mother; the court granted fifty bolts of silk and fifty piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 昭性至孝，明宗聞其居喪哀毀，復賜以錢幣。

translations.literal: Zhao by nature was extremely filial; when Mingzong heard of his grief and emaciation in mourning, he again bestowed money.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was deeply filial by nature. When Mingzong heard how he grieved and wasted away in mourning, he sent money again.

sentences.zh: 服除，改職方員外郎、知制誥，充史館修撰。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was changed to Vice Director of the Bureau of Equipment, drafter of edicts, and served as History Office compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Vice Director of the Bureau of Equipment, drafter of edicts, and History Office compiler.

sentences.zh: 上言乞復本朝故事，置觀察使察民疾苦，御史彈事，諫官月給諫紙。

translations.literal: He submitted asking to restore this court's former practices: establish surveillance commissioners to inspect the people's hardships, censors to impeach matters, and remonstrance officials to receive monthly remonstrance paper.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to restore former practice: surveillance commissioners to inspect popular hardship, censors to impeach wrongdoing, and remonstrance officials given monthly remonstrance paper.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 又奏請勸農耕及置常平倉等數事。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting encouragement of farming and establishment of ever-normal granaries, among several matters.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to encourage farming and establish ever-normal granaries, among other measures.

sentences.zh: 明宗方務聽納，昭復上疏曰：「臣聞『安不忘危，治不忘亂』者，先儒之丕訓；

translations.literal: Mingzong was then striving to heed and accept advice; Zhao again submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that 'in security do not forget peril, in order do not forget disorder' is the great teaching of the former Confucians;
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was then eager to listen. Zhao submitted another memorial: "I have heard that 'in peace do not forget danger, in order do not forget chaos' is the great teaching of the ancients;

sentences.zh: 『靡不有初，鮮克有終』者，前經之至戒。

translations.literal: 'Few things lack a beginning, few can keep the end' is the utmost warning of the former classics.
translations.idiomatic: 'All things have a beginning, few keep the end' is the sternest warning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 究觀列辟，莫不以驕矜怠惰，有虧盛德。

translations.literal: Examining all rulers, none failed to diminish their great virtue through pride, arrogance, idleness, and sloth.
translations.idiomatic: Look at every ruler: all diminished their great virtue through pride, arrogance, and sloth.

sentences.zh: 恭惟太宗貞觀之初，玄宗開元之際，焦勞庶政，以致太平。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering the beginning of Emperor Taizong's Zhenguan and the time of Emperor Xuanzong's Kaiyuan, they toiled anxiously over the myriad affairs of government and thereby achieved great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Emperor Taizong at the start of Zhenguan and Emperor Xuanzong in early Kaiyuan: they labored over government until peace came.

sentences.zh: 及國富兵消，年高志逸，乃忽守約之道，或貽執簡之譏。

translations.literal: When the state was rich and arms at rest, their years advanced and their wills grew lax—they then neglected the way of keeping covenant and sometimes incurred the reproach of those who hold the bamboo slips.
translations.idiomatic: When the state grew rich and arms idle, they grew old and their wills wandered; they neglected restraint and earned the historians' reproach.

sentences.zh: 陛下以慈儉化天下，以禮法檢臣鄰，絀奸邪之黨，延正直之論，務遵純儉，以節浮費，信賞必罰，至公無私。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with kindness and frugality transforms the realm, with ritual and law restrains ministers and neighbors, dismisses factions of the wicked, extends discussions of the upright, strives to follow pure frugality to curtail wasteful expense, and in rewards and punishments is faithful, certain, utterly public, and without private bias.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty transforms the realm through kindness and frugality, restrains ministers with ritual and law, dismisses wicked factions, welcomes upright counsel, keeps to plain thrift, cuts waste, and in reward and punishment is faithful, certain, and utterly fair.

sentences.zh: 其創業垂統之基，如貞觀、開元之始，然陛下有始有終，無荒無怠。

translations.literal: The foundation of founding the enterprise and bequeathing the succession is like the beginning of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan—yet may Your Majesty have beginning and end, without dissipation and without sloth.
translations.idiomatic: Your foundation for founding and bequeathing the dynasty is like early Zhenguan and Kaiyuan—only may Your Majesty keep beginning and end, never slacken, never grow idle.

sentences.zh: 臣又伏念保邦之道，有八審焉，願為陛下陳之：夫委任審於材器，聽受審於忠邪，出令審於煩苛，興師審於德力，賞罰審於喜怒，毀譽審於愛憎，議論審於賢愚，嬖寵審於奸佞。

translations.literal: Your subject again humbly reflects that in the way of preserving the state there are eight scrutinies; he wishes to set them forth for Your Majesty: entrustment scrutinized by talent and capacity, listening scrutinized by loyalty and treachery, issuing orders scrutinized by vexation and severity, raising armies scrutinized by virtue and strength, rewards and punishments scrutinized by joy and anger, praise and blame scrutinized by love and hate, discussion scrutinized by worth and folly, favor scrutinized by the wicked and the sycophantic.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect again that preserving the state requires eight careful judgments, which I wish to lay before Your Majesty: entrust office by talent; listen by loyalty or treachery; issue orders by whether they burden or oppress; raise armies by moral strength; reward and punish apart from mood; weigh praise and blame apart from affection; judge debate by wisdom or folly; grant favor apart from flatterers.

sentences.zh: 推是八審，以決萬機，庶可以臻至治。」

translations.literal: Apply these eight scrutinies to decide the myriad affairs, and one may perhaps reach supreme order."
translations.idiomatic: Apply these eight judgments to the myriad affairs of state, and you may reach supreme order."

sentences.zh: 明宗覽之稱善。

translations.literal: Mingzong read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong read it and praised it.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，改駕部郎中、知制誥，撰皇后冊文，遷中書舍人，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, he was changed to Director of the Bureau of Transport, drafter of edicts, composed the empress's investiture text, was promoted to Attendant Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qingtai he was made Director of the Bureau of Transport and drafter of edicts, wrote the empress's investiture document, was promoted to Secretariat drafting secretary, and was granted gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 二年，加判史館兼點閱三館書籍，校正添補。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was additionally made overseer of the History Office and inspector of the books of the Three Institutes, correcting and supplementing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was additionally made overseer of the History Office and inspector of the Three Institutes' books, correcting and supplementing them.

sentences.zh: 預修《明宗實錄》，成三十卷以獻。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Mingzong, completed thirty juan, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Mingzong, finished thirty juan, and presented them.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷禮部侍郎，改御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and changed to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Vice Minister of Rites and then Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，從幸汴州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu under Jin, he followed the imperial progress to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianfu under Later Jin he accompanied the emperor to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭請創宮闕名額及振舉朝綱、條疏百司廨舍。

translations.literal: Zhao requested to establish names and plaques for the palace halls, revive the court's standards, and itemize the offices and government compounds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao asked to name the palace halls, restore court discipline, and list the offices and government compounds.

sentences.zh: 二年，改戶部侍郎，宰相桑維翰薦為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was changed to Vice Minister of Revenue; the chief minister Sang Weihan recommended him as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Chief Minister Sang Weihan recommended him as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 內署故事，以先後入為次，不繫官序，特詔昭立位次承旨崔棁。

translations.literal: By precedent of the inner secretariat, precedence followed order of entry, not official rank; a special edict ordered Zhao to take standing after Chief Drafting Secretary Cui Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: By inner secretariat custom, seniority followed date of entry, not rank; a special edict placed Zhao after Chief Drafting Secretary Cui Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 晉祖嘗幸內署，與昭語及幷、魏舊事，甚重之，錫賚頗厚。

translations.literal: The Jin founder once visited the inner secretariat, conversed with Zhao about old matters of Bing and Wei, valued him greatly, and bestowed generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder once visited the inner secretariat, talked with Zhao about old affairs in Bing and Wei, thought highly of him, and gave him rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 直以昭故，授著作佐郎致仕，至是卒。

translations.literal: Because of Zhao, Zhi was granted retirement as Assistant Compiler; at this time he died.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Zhao, Zhi had been granted retirement as Assistant Compiler; he died at this time.

sentences.zh: 歸西洛，賻賜加等。

translations.literal: When he returned to the western Luo capital, condolence gifts were increased in grade.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao returned to Luoyang, condolence gifts were increased.

sentences.zh: 五年，服闋，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the mourning period ended, he was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, once his mourning obligations were fulfilled, he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以唐史未成，詔與呂琦、崔棁等續成之，別置史院，命昭兼判院事。

translations.literal: Because the Tang history had not yet been completed, an edict ordered him, together with Lu Qi, Cui Zhuo, and others, to continue and finish it; a separate History Institute was established, and Zhao was ordered to serve concurrently as its chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: As the Tang history remained unfinished, the court ordered him, Lu Qi, Cui Zhuo, and others to carry the work to completion. A separate History Institute was established, and Zhao was put in charge of it as well.

sentences.zh: 昭又撰《唐朝君臣正論》二十五卷上之。

translations.literal: Zhao also compiled and submitted Correct Discussions on Tang Rulers and Ministers in twenty-five juan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also wrote Correct Discussions on Tang Rulers and Ministers in twenty-five scrolls and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the post of Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷吏部，判東銓，兼史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, put in charge of the eastern selection board, and concurrently served as a compiler of the History Office and administrator of its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, given charge of the eastern selection board, and at the same time made a History Office compiler and head of its administration.

sentences.zh: 開運二年秋，《唐書》成二百卷，加金紫階，進爵邑。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyun, the Book of Tang was completed in two hundred juan; he was granted the gold-and-purple rank and received advancement in title and fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyun, the Book of Tang was finished in two hundred scrolls. He was awarded the gold-and-purple insignia and promoted in rank and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜尚書右丞，判流內銓，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, put in charge of the internal selection board, and given provisional authority over the imperial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, given charge of the internal selection board, and entrusted with provisional oversight of the imperial examinations.

sentences.zh: 漢初，復為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Later Han, he again became Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han dynasty was founded, he was again appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時追尊六廟，定諡號、樂章、舞曲，命昭權判太常卿事，月餘即真。

translations.literal: At that time, as the court was posthumously honoring the six ancestral temples and fixing posthumous titles, ritual music, and dance pieces, Zhao was ordered to serve provisionally as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; after a little more than a month he received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was raising posthumous honors in the six ancestral temples and settling imperial titles, ritual hymns, and dance music. Zhao was ordered to serve provisionally as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and after little more than a month received the regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 乾佑二年，加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyou, he was additionally made Inspector General of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyou he was further given the honorary title of Inspector General of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 少帝年十九，猶有童心，昵比群小。

translations.literal: The young emperor was nineteen years old and still possessed a childish heart; he kept close company with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor was only nineteen and still had the mind of a boy; he kept intimate company with low companions.

sentences.zh: 昭上言請聽政之暇，數召儒臣講論經義。

translations.literal: Zhao memorialized the throne, asking that in the intervals when the emperor was not hearing affairs of state, Confucian officials be frequently summoned to lecture on and discuss the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao submitted a memorial asking that, whenever the emperor had leisure from governing, learned officials be summoned often to lecture on the classics and discuss their meaning.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun under the Later Zhou, he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Guangshun era under the Later Zhou, he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子秉陽，為陽翟主簿，抵罪，昭自以失教，奉表引咎，左遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: His son Bingyang, who was chief clerk of Yangdi, was convicted of a crime. Zhao, holding himself responsible for failure in instruction, submitted a memorial accepting blame and was demoted to Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingyang, then chief clerk of Yangdi, was found guilty of an offense. Zhao, believing himself at fault for poor upbringing, submitted a memorial taking blame upon himself and was demoted to Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復舊官。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After a little over a year, he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏請興制舉，設賢良方正能直言極諫、經學優深可為師法、詳閑吏治達於教化三科，職官、士流、黃衣、草澤並許應詔。

translations.literal: He once memorialized requesting the revival of the special decree examinations, establishing three categories: Worthy and Upright, Able to Speak Bluntly and Offer Extreme Remonstrance; Profound in Classical Learning and Fit to Serve as a Model for Teaching; and Thoroughly Versed in Official Administration and Adept in Transforming the People through Education. Officials in active service, members of the scholar-gentry, candidates in yellow robes, and commoners from the wilds were all permitted to respond to the imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized asking that the special decree examinations be revived, with three categories established: Worthy and Upright, Able to Speak Bluntly and Offer Extreme Remonstrance; Profound in Classical Learning and Fit to Serve as a Model for Teaching; and Thoroughly Versed in Official Administration and Adept in Transforming the People through Education. Serving officials, gentry candidates, yellow-robed examinees, and commoners from every quarter were all to be allowed to answer the imperial call.

sentences.zh: 諸州依貢舉體式，量試策論三道，共以三千字以上為準，考其文理俱優，解送尚書吏部，其登朝之官亦聽自舉。

translations.literal: The various prefectures, following the form of the regular tribute examinations, were to set written policy essays in three topics, taking more than three thousand characters in total as the standard; those whose literary and reasoning were both excellent were to be sent on to the Ministry of Personnel, and officials already at court were also permitted to recommend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures, following the format of the regular tribute examinations, were to set three policy essays, with a combined minimum of three thousand characters; candidates whose writing and reasoning were both outstanding were to be forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel, and officials already serving at court were also allowed to enter on their own initiative.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande, he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiande he was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 世宗以昭舊德，甚重焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because of Zhao's long-standing virtue, held him in very high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, honoring Zhao for his long service and moral standing, held him in the highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 二年，表求致仕，優詔不允，促其入謁。

translations.literal: In the second year, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; a gracious edict refused permission and urged him to come to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he submitted a memorial asking to retire; the emperor issued a gracious edict refusing permission and pressed him to attend court.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔撰《制旨兵法》十卷，又撰《周祖實錄》三十卷，及梁郢王、均帝、後唐閔帝、廢帝、漢隱帝五朝實錄；

translations.literal: He was once ordered to compile Imperial Military Methods in ten juan, and also compiled Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu of Zhou in thirty juan, as well as the veritable records of five reigns: the Liang Prince of Ying, the Jun Emperor, the Later Tang Emperor Min, the Deposed Emperor, and the Later Han Emperor Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to compile Imperial Military Methods in ten scrolls, and also wrote Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu of Zhou in thirty scrolls, together with the veritable records of five reigns: the Liang Prince of Ying, the Jun Emperor, the Later Tang Emperor Min, the Deposed Emperor, and the Later Han Emperor Yin.

sentences.zh: 梁二主年祀浸遠，事皆遺失，遂不克修，餘三帝實錄，皆藏史閣。

translations.literal: The two Liang rulers had receded far into the past and their affairs were largely lost, so those records could not be completed; the veritable records of the other three emperors were all stored in the History Archive.
translations.idiomatic: The two Liang rulers lay too far back in time and their affairs had largely been lost, so those records could not be completed; the veritable records of the other three emperors were all deposited in the History Archive.

sentences.zh: 世宗好拔奇俊，有自布衣及下位上書言事者，多不次進用。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong loved to elevate extraordinary talent; when men from commoner status or low office submitted memorials on public affairs, many were promoted out of regular order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong delighted in raising extraordinary men of talent; when commoners or officials of low rank submitted memorials on state affairs, many were promoted ahead of their proper turn.

sentences.zh: 昭疏諫曰：「昔唐初，劉洎、馬周起於徒步，太宗擢用為相；

translations.literal: Zhao submitted a remonstrance saying: "In early Tang, Liu Ji and Ma Zhou rose from common walks, and Emperor Taizong elevated and employed them as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao submitted a remonstrance, saying: "In early Tang, Liu Ji and Ma Zhou rose from humble walks of life, and Emperor Taizong elevated them and made them chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 其後，柳璨、朱朴方居下僚，昭宗亦加大用。

translations.literal: Later, Liu Can and Zhu Pu had only just occupied lower posts, yet Emperor Zhaozong also gave them great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Liu Can and Zhu Pu were still in subordinate posts when Emperor Zhaozong likewise put them to great use.

sentences.zh: 此四士者，受知於明主；

translations.literal: These four men all won recognition from enlightened rulers.
translations.idiomatic: All four of these men won the trust of enlightened sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 然太宗用之而國興，昭宗用之而國亡，士之難知如此。

translations.literal: Yet Taizong employed them and the state flourished, while Zhaozong employed them and the state perished — so difficult is it to know men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taizong employed them and the realm prospered, while Zhaozong employed them and the realm was lost. Knowing men is indeed so difficult.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下存舊法而用人，當以此四士為鑒戒。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty, in preserving the old methods of employing men, take these four men as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty, in keeping to the established methods of employing men, to take these four men as a warning."

sentences.zh: 世宗善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong approved of the advice.

sentences.zh: 詔令詳定《經典釋文》、《九經文字》、《制科條式》，及問六璽所出，並議《三禮圖》祭玉及鼎釜等。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a detailed revision of Exegesis of the Classics, Characters of the Nine Classics, Regulations for the Decree Examination, and inquiry into the origins of the six imperial seals, together with deliberation on the jade and cauldrons used in sacrifice according to Illustrations of the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a detailed revision of Exegesis of the Classics, Characters of the Nine Classics, and the regulations for the decree examination, inquiry into the origins of the six imperial seals, and deliberation on the sacrificial jades and cauldrons in Illustrations of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 昭援引經據，時稱其該博。

translations.literal: Zhao cited classics and evidence in support, and at the time he was praised for the breadth of his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cited classical texts and evidence in support of his views, and contemporaries praised the breadth of his erudition.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，封舒國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong ascended the throne, Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong came to the throne, Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 宋初，拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Early in Song he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年郊祀，昭為鹵簿使，奏復宮闕、廟門、郊壇夜警晨嚴之制。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice in the first year of Qiande, Zhao served as master of the guard of honor and memorialized for the restoration of the regulations for night watch and morning salute at the palace, temple gates, and suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice in the first year of Qiande, Zhao served as master of the guard of honor and memorialized for the restoration of the regulations for night watch and morning salute at the palace, temple gates, and suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，進封鄭國公，與翰林承旨陶穀同掌選。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete he was advanced to Duke of Zheng and, with Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Tao Gu, jointly managed selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete he was advanced to Duke of Zheng and, with Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Tao Gu, jointly managed selection.

sentences.zh: 穀嘗誣奏事，引昭為證，昭免冠抗論。

translations.literal: Gu once falsely reported an affair and cited Zhao as witness; Zhao removed his cap and argued against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu once falsely reported an affair and cited Zhao as witness; Zhao removed his cap and argued against him.

sentences.zh: 太祖不說，遂三拜章告老，以本官致仕，改封陳國公。

translations.literal: Taizu was displeased, so Zhao thrice submitted memorials requesting retirement, retired in his existing rank, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was displeased, so Zhao thrice submitted memorials requesting retirement, retired in his existing rank, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 昭博通學術，書無不覽，兼善天文、風角、太一、卜相、兵法、釋老之說，藏書數萬卷。

translations.literal: Zhao was broadly learned in scholarship and read every book without exception; he was also skilled in astronomy, wind divination, Taiyi numerology, physiognomy, military strategy, and Buddhist and Daoist teachings, and his library numbered tens of thousands of juan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was broadly learned and read without exception; he was also adept at astronomy, wind divination, Taiyi numerology, physiognomy, military strategy, and Buddhist and Daoist doctrine, and his private library ran to tens of thousands of scrolls.

sentences.zh: 尤好纂述，自唐、晉至宋，專筆削典章之任。

translations.literal: He especially loved compilation and editing; from Tang and Jin through to Song, he devoted himself to the task of drafting and revising canonical statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to compilation and editing; from Tang and Jin down to Song, he held the brush in matters of canonical law and institutional record.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，擒劉鋹，將獻俘，莫能知其禮。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified and Liu Chang was captured, the court was about to present the captives, but no one knew the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingnan was pacified and Liu Chang was taken captive, the court prepared to present the prisoners, but no one knew the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 時昭已致政，太祖遣近臣就其家問之，昭方臥病，口占以授使者。

translations.literal: By then Zhao had already retired from office; Taizu sent a close attendant to his home to ask him. Zhao was then ill in bed and dictated the answer for the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhao had already retired; Taizu sent a close attendant to his home to inquire. Zhao was then bedridden with illness and dictated his answer for the messenger.

sentences.zh: 著《嘉善集》五十卷、《名臣事跡》五卷。

translations.literal: He authored Collection from Jiashan in fifty juan and Records of Eminent Ministers in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collection from Jiashan in fifty scrolls and Records of Eminent Ministers in five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子秉圖進士及第；

translations.literal: His son Bingtu passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingtu passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 秉謙至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Bingqian rose to the rank of Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Bingqian rose to become a Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 竇儀，字可象。

translations.literal: Dou Yi, styled Kexiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi, courtesy name Kexiang.

sentences.zh: 薊州漁陽人。

translations.literal: A native of Yuyang in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was a native of Yuyang in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖遜，玉田令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xun was magistrate of Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xun served as magistrate of Yutian.

sentences.zh: 祖思恭，媯州司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sigong was Assistant Military Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sigong was Assistant Military Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 父禹鈞，與兄禹錫皆以詞學名。

translations.literal: His father Yujun, together with his elder brother Yuxi, were both famed for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yujun, together with his elder brother Yuxi, were both renowned for literary scholarship.

sentences.zh: 禹鈞，唐天佑末起家幽州掾，歷沂、鄧、安、同、鄭、華、宋、澶州支使判官。

translations.literal: Yujun, at the end of the Tianyou era of Tang, began his career as an aide in Youzhou and successively served as administrative aide and judicial aide in the prefectures of Yi, Deng, An, Tong, Zheng, Hua, Song, and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Yujun entered service at the end of the Tianyou era as an aide in Youzhou, and thereafter served successively as administrative and judicial aide in Yi, Deng, An, Tong, Zheng, Hua, Song, and Cao.

sentences.zh: 周初，為戶部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhou, he became Director in the Ministry of Revenue and was granted the gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Later Zhou he became a Director in the Ministry of Revenue and was awarded the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，遷太常少卿、右諫議大夫致仕。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Right Reminder of the Censorate, then retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Right Reminder of the Censorate, then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 儀十五能屬文，晉天福中舉進士。

translations.literal: Yi, at fifteen, could compose literary pieces, and in the Tianfu era of Jin he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Yi could already compose essays, and during the Tianfu era of Jin he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 侍衛軍帥景延廣領夔州節度，表為記室。

translations.literal: Jing Yanguang, commander of the Palace Guard, also held the Kuizhou military governorship and recommended Yi as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yanguang, commander of the Palace Guard, concurrently held the Kuizhou governorship and recommended Yi as his recorder.

sentences.zh: 延廣後歷滑、陝、孟、鄆四鎮，儀並為從事。

translations.literal: Yanguang later successively held the four prefectures of Hua, Shan, Meng, and Yan, and Yi served as his staff officer throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang later served in succession at the four prefectures of Hua, Shan, Meng, and Yan, and Yi accompanied him as staff officer throughout.

sentences.zh: 開運中，楊光遠以青州叛，時契丹南侵，博州刺史周儒以城降，光遠與儒遣人引契丹輕騎於馬家渡渡河。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era, Yang Guangyuan rebelled at Qingzhou. At that time the Khitan were invading from the south; Zhou Ru, prefect of Bozhou, surrendered the city. Guangyuan and Ru sent men to guide Khitan light cavalry across the river at Majia Ford.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun era Yang Guangyuan rebelled at Qingzhou. The Khitan were then invading from the south; Zhou Ru, prefect of Bozhou, surrendered his city. Guangyuan and Ru sent men to guide Khitan light cavalry across the river at Majia Ford.

sentences.zh: 時延廣掌衛兵，顏衎知州事，即遣儀入奏。

translations.literal: At that time Yanguang commanded the palace troops, and Yan Kan was acting prefect; they immediately sent Yi to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang then commanded the palace troops, and Yan Kan was acting prefect; they immediately dispatched Yi to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 儀謂執政曰：「昨與衎論事勢，有所預慮，所以乘驛晝夜不息而來。

translations.literal: Yi said to those in power: "Yesterday, in discussing the situation with Kan, I had certain forebodings, and therefore rode post day and night without rest to come here.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said to the chief ministers: "Yesterday, when Kan and I discussed the situation, I had certain forebodings, and so I rode post day and night without pause to reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 國家若不以良將重兵控博州渡，必恐儒引契丹逾東岸與光遠兵合，則河南危矣。」

translations.literal: If the state does not send good generals with strong forces to control the Bozhou crossing, I fear Ru will surely guide the Khitan beyond the eastern bank to join with Guangyuan's army, and then Henan will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not send able generals with heavy forces to hold the Bozhou crossing, I fear Ru will surely lead the Khitan beyond the eastern bank to join Guangyuan's army, and then Henan will be in grave danger."

sentences.zh: 俄而儒果導契丹渡河，增置壘柵。

translations.literal: Before long Ru indeed guided the Khitan across the river and added fortifications and palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ru did indeed guide the Khitan across the river and began building fortifications and palisades.

sentences.zh: 少帝軍河上，即遣李守貞等率兵萬人，水陸並進，守汶陽，據要害。

translations.literal: The young emperor's army was on the Yellow River; he immediately sent Li Shouzhen and others to lead ten thousand men by land and water together, to hold Wenyang and occupy the strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor's army was stationed on the Yellow River; he immediately sent Li Shouzhen and others with ten thousand men advancing by land and water to hold Wenyang and seize the critical positions.

sentences.zh: 契丹果大至，擊走之。

translations.literal: The Khitan indeed arrived in force and were driven off.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan did arrive in force, but were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 漢初，召為左補闕、禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Later Han, he was summoned as Left Reminder and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Later Han he was summoned to serve as Left Reminder and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，改倉部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun under the Later Zhou, he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Granaries and put in charge of drafting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Guangshun under the Later Zhou he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Granaries and put in charge of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Before long, he was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 周祖幸南御莊宴射，坐中賜金紫。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu of Zhou, on visiting the Southern Imperial Estate for archery and feasting, granted him the gold-and-purple insignia while seated at the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou visited the Southern Imperial Estate for an archery feast, he granted Yi the gold-and-purple insignia there at table.

sentences.zh: 歷駕部郎中、給事中，並充職。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director in the Ministry of Transport and as Supervising Censor, while continuing in his concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Director in the Ministry of Transport and as Supervising Censor, while retaining his concurrent appointments.

sentences.zh: 劉溫叟知貢舉，所取士有覆落者，加儀禮部侍郎，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: Liu Wensou was superintendent of the imperial examinations, and among those he selected were candidates who failed re-examination; Yi was added as Vice Minister of Rites and given provisional authority over the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wensou was superintendent of the imperial examinations, but some of the candidates he selected failed re-examination; Yi was therefore made Vice Minister of Rites and given provisional charge of the examinations.

sentences.zh: 儀上言：「請依晉天福五年制，廢明經、童子科。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized: "I request that, following the regulation of the fifth year of Tianfu under Jin, the Mingjing and Youth examinations be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized: "I ask that, in accordance with the regulation of the fifth year of Tianfu under Jin, the Mingjing and Youth examinations be abolished.

sentences.zh: 進士省卷，令納五軸以上，不得有神道碑誌之類；

translations.literal: For the jinshi examination, submitted papers must contain five scrolls or more, and must not include spirit-way stele inscriptions or the like.
translations.idiomatic: For the jinshi examination, candidates must submit five scrolls or more, and must not include spirit-way stele inscriptions or the like.

sentences.zh: 帖經對義，有三通為合格；

translations.literal: In the classic-text matching and meaning-explanation section, passing three of the sets qualifies.
translations.idiomatic: In the classic-text matching and meaning-explanation section, success in three sets constitutes a pass.

sentences.zh: 卻復盡試。

translations.literal: Then all are tested again in full.
translations.idiomatic: All candidates are then tested again in full.

sentences.zh: 其落第者，分為五等：以詞理紕繆之甚者為第五等，殿五舉；

translations.literal: Those who fail are divided into five grades: those whose wording and reasoning are most confused are placed in the fifth grade and barred for five examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fail are divided into five grades: those whose language and reasoning are most confused are placed in the fifth grade and barred from five examinations.

sentences.zh: 其次為第四等，殿三舉；

translations.literal: Next come the fourth grade, barred for three examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Next is the fourth grade, barred for three examinations.

sentences.zh: 以次稍可者為第三、第二、第一等，並許次年赴舉。

translations.literal: Those somewhat better in descending order are placed in the third, second, and first grades, and all are permitted to take the examination again the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Those somewhat better, in descending order, are placed in the third, second, and first grades, and all are allowed to sit again the following year.

sentences.zh: 其學究，請並《周易》、《尚書》為一科，各對墨義三十道；

translations.literal: As for the Xuejiu scholars, I request that the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents be combined into one category, each with thirty written meaning questions.
translations.idiomatic: For the Xuejiu scholars, I ask that the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents be combined into one category, each with thirty written meaning questions.

sentences.zh: 《毛詩》依舊為一科，亦對墨義六十道。

translations.literal: The Book of Poetry is to remain a separate category, likewise with sixty written meaning questions.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry is to remain a separate category, also with sixty written meaning questions.

sentences.zh: 及第後，並減為七選集。

translations.literal: After passing, all are reduced to seven rounds of selection for office.
translations.idiomatic: After passing, all are reduced to seven rounds of waiting for appointment.

sentences.zh: 諸科舉人，第一場十否，殿五舉；

translations.literal: For candidates in the various examinations, ten failures in the first session bar one for five examinations.
translations.idiomatic: For candidates in the various examinations, ten failures in the first session bar one from five examinations.

sentences.zh: 第二、第三場十否，殿三舉；

translations.literal: Ten failures in the second or third session bar one for three examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Ten failures in the second or third session bar one from three examinations.

sentences.zh: 三場內有九否，殿一舉。

translations.literal: Nine failures within the three sessions bar one for one examination.
translations.idiomatic: Nine failures across the three sessions bar one from one examination.

sentences.zh: 解試之官坐其罪。

translations.literal: The official who presided over the qualifying examination is punished according to the offense.
translations.idiomatic: The official who presided over the qualifying examination is punished according to the offense.

sentences.zh: 進士請解，加試論一首，以五百言以上為準。」

translations.literal: For jinshi candidates seeking qualification, add one policy essay, taking five hundred characters or more as the standard."
translations.idiomatic: For jinshi candidates seeking qualification, add one policy essay, with a minimum of five hundred characters."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 俄以父病，上表解官。

translations.literal: Before long, because his father was ill, he submitted a memorial requesting release from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on account of his father's illness, he submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 世宗親加慰撫，手封金丹，俾賜其父。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong personally added words of consolation, sealed golden pills with his own hand, and ordered that they be given to his father.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong personally wrote words of consolation, sealed golden pills with his own hand, and ordered them sent to his father.

sentences.zh: 父卒，歸葬洛陽。

translations.literal: When his father died, he returned to bury him in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he returned home to bury him in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔賜錢三十萬，米麥三百斛。

translations.literal: An edict granted thirty thousand strings of cash and three hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted thirty thousand strings of cash and three hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 終喪，召拜端明殿學士。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was summoned and appointed Academician of the Hall of Enduring Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete, he was summoned and appointed Academician of the Hall of Enduring Brightness.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，判行在三司，世宗以其餉饋不繼，將罪之，宰相范質救解得免。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Huainan, he was put in charge of the field headquarters of the Three Departments; because supplies were not continuous, Emperor Shizong was about to punish him, but the chief minister Fan Zhi interceded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huainan campaign he was put in charge of the field headquarters of the Three Departments. Because supplies failed to keep up, Emperor Shizong was about to punish him, but Chief Minister Fan Zhi interceded and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，判河南府兼知西京留守事。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, he was put in charge of Henan Prefecture and concurrently given authority over the western capital as acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, he was put in charge of Henan Prefecture and concurrently given authority over the western capital as acting regent.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，遷兵部侍郎，充職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of War and continued in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong came to the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of War and continued in office.

sentences.zh: 俄使南唐，既至，將宣詔，會雨雪，李景請於廡下拜受，儀曰：「儀獲將國命，不敢失舊禮。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent as envoy to Southern Tang. After arriving, just as he was about to proclaim the edict, snow and rain set in. Li Jing asked to receive it beneath the corridor, but Yi said: "Yi has received the charge of the state's command and dare not depart from the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent as envoy to Southern Tang. After his arrival, just as he was about to proclaim the edict, snow and rain began to fall. Li Jing asked to receive it beneath the corridor, but Yi said: "I bear the command of the state and dare not depart from established ritual.

sentences.zh: 儻以沾服失容，請俟他日。」

translations.literal: If receiving it in wet garments would spoil proper bearing, please wait for another day."
translations.idiomatic: If receiving it in wet garments would mar proper bearing, let us wait for another day."

sentences.zh: 景即拜命於庭。

translations.literal: Jing then received the command in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing then received the command in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年秋，遷工部尚書，罷學士，兼判大理寺。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Jianlong, he was transferred to Minister of Works, removed from the Hanlin Academy, and concurrently put in charge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Jianlong he was transferred to Minister of Works, relieved of his Hanlin post, and concurrently put in charge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 奉詔重定《刑統》，為三十卷。

translations.literal: By imperial order he revised the Penal Code, making it thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he revised the Penal Code, producing a work of thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 會翰林學士王著以酒失貶官，太祖謂宰相曰：「深嚴之地，當待宿儒處之。」

translations.literal: When Hanlin Academician Wang Zhu was demoted for a lapse involving wine, Taizu said to the chief ministers: "In so solemn a place, one ought to place a seasoned scholar."
translations.idiomatic: When Hanlin Academician Wang Zhu was demoted for a drunken offense, Taizu said to the chief ministers: "In so solemn a place, one ought to place a seasoned scholar."

sentences.zh: 范質等對曰：「竇儀清介重厚，然已自翰林遷端明矣。」

translations.literal: Fan Zhi and the others replied: "Dou Yi is upright, incorruptible, and weighty in character, but he has already moved from the Hanlin Academy to the Hall of Enduring Brightness."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi and the others replied: "Dou Yi is upright, incorruptible, and weighty in character, but he has already moved from the Hanlin Academy to the Hall of Enduring Brightness."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「非斯人不可處禁中，卿當諭以朕意，勉令就職。」

translations.literal: Taizu said: "No one but this man can occupy the forbidden precinct; you should convey my intent and earnestly urge him to take office."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said: "No one but this man can occupy the forbidden precinct; you should convey my intent and earnestly urge him to take office."

sentences.zh: 即日再入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: That same day he re-entered the Hanlin Academy as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he re-entered the Hanlin Academy as Academician.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，范質等三相並罷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, Fan Zhi and the other three chief ministers were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, Fan Zhi and the other three chief ministers were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 越三日，始命趙普平章事。

translations.literal: Three days later, Zhao Pu alone was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Three days passed before Zhao Pu alone was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 制書既下，太祖問翰林學士曰：「質等已罷，普敕何官當署？」

translations.literal: Once the appointment edict had been issued, Taizu asked the Hanlin academicians: "Fan Zhi and the others have already been dismissed — which office should sign Zhao Pu's appointment edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Once the appointment edict had been issued, Taizu asked the Hanlin academicians: "Fan Zhi and the others have already been dismissed — which office should sign Zhao Pu's appointment edict?"

sentences.zh: 承旨陶穀時任尚書，乃建議相位不可以久虛，今尚書乃南省六官之長，可以署敕。

translations.literal: The chief drafter Tao Gu, then serving as Minister, proposed that the chancellor's seat could not long remain vacant; the Minister was now head of the six bureaus of the outer secretariat and could countersign edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Gu, the chief drafter who was then Minister of Works, argued that the chancellorship ought not stand empty for long—the Minister, as head of the six offices of the outer court, was fit to countersign imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「穀所陳非承平之制，皇弟開封尹、同平章事，即宰相之任。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "What Gu has put forward is not the institution of settled times. The Emperor's younger brother, Grand Prefect of Kaifeng and Vice Grand Councilor—that is the chancellor's charge."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi replied, "What Gu proposes is no institution for a time of peace. The Emperor's younger brother, Prefect of Kaifeng and Vice Grand Councilor—that is already the chancellor's office."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「儀言是也。」

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "Yi's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Yi is right."

sentences.zh: 即命太宗署敕賜之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the Taizong to countersign the edict and grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered Taizong to countersign the edict and issue the appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄加禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was additionally appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was further appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時御史臺議，欲以左右僕射合為表首，太常禮院以東宮三師為表首。

translations.literal: At the time the Censorate debated making the Left and Right Vice Directors jointly the head of memorial tables, while the Directorate of Ceremonies held that the Three Preceptors of the Eastern Palace should head the tables.
