translations.idiomatic: The Censorate then debated whether the Left and Right Vice Directors together should head official memorial rolls, while the Directorate of Ceremonies maintained that the Three Preceptors of the Eastern Palace should take precedence.

sentences.zh: 儀援典故，以僕射合為表首者六，而謂三師無所據。

translations.literal: Yi cited precedent: there were six instances of Vice Directors jointly heading tables, while he argued the Three Preceptors had no basis in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi invoked precedent, noting six cases in which the Vice Directors jointly headed the rolls, and argued that the Three Preceptors had no documentary warrant.

sentences.zh: 朝議是之。

translations.literal: Court opinion agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sided with him.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year he supervised the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year he was put in charge of the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 是冬卒，年五十三，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged fifty-three, and was posthumously awarded the title of Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter at fifty-three and was posthumously ennobled as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 儀學問優博，風度峻整。

translations.literal: Yi was broad and superior in learning, stern and dignified in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi was deeply learned and broad in scholarship, with a grave and commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 弟儼、侃、偁、僖，皆相繼登科。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Yan, Kan, Cheng, and Xi all passed the examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Yan, Kan, Cheng, and Xi all passed the examinations, one after another.

sentences.zh: 馮道與禹鈞有舊，嘗贈詩，有「靈椿一株老，丹桂五枝芳」之句，縉紳多諷誦之，當時號為「竇氏五龍」。

translations.literal: Feng Dao had old ties with Yujun and once presented a poem containing the lines, "One sacred catalpa grows old; five cassia boughs bloom fragrant." Officials often recited it, and at the time they were called "the Five Dragons of the Dou Clan."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao, who had long known Dou Yujun, once sent him a poem with the lines, "One sacred catalpa stands in age; five cassia branches flower in splendor." Courtiers recited it widely, and the brothers were known in their day as "the Five Dragons of the Dou Clan."

sentences.zh: 初，周祖平兗州，議將盡誅脅從者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Zhou founder pacified Yanzhou, there was discussion of executing all who had been coerced into following.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Zhou founder pacified Yanzhou, some proposed putting to death everyone who had been forced to follow the rebels.

sentences.zh: 儀白馮道、范質，同請於周祖，皆得全活。

translations.literal: Yi informed Feng Dao and Fan Zhi; together they pleaded before the Zhou founder, and all were spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi told Feng Dao and Fan Zhi, and together they petitioned the Zhou founder; all were spared.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，太祖克滁州，世宗遣儀籍其府庫。

translations.literal: During the Xiande reign, after Taizu captured Chuzhou, Shizong sent Yi to register its treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era, after Taizu took Chuzhou, Shizong dispatched Dou Yi to inventory the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 太祖復令親吏取藏中絹給麾下，儀曰：「太尉初下城，雖傾藏以給軍士，誰敢言者。

translations.literal: Taizu again ordered a personal clerk to take silk from the storehouses to supply his troops. Yi said, "When the Grand Marshal first took the city, even if he emptied the stores to supply the soldiers, who would have dared speak?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then ordered one of his personal clerks to take silk from the registered stores for his troops. Yi said, "When the Grand Marshal first entered the city, he might have emptied the treasury to pay the soldiers—and who would have dared object?

sentences.zh: 今既著籍，乃公帑物也，非詔不可取。」

translations.literal: Now that it has been entered in the registers, it is public treasury property; without an imperial edict it may not be taken."
translations.idiomatic: But now that it has been entered in the books, it is public treasury property. Without an imperial order it cannot be taken."

sentences.zh: 後太祖屢對大臣稱儀有執守，欲相之。

translations.literal: Later Taizu repeatedly told the chief ministers that Yi had integrity and wished to make him chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Taizu repeatedly told his ministers that Yi was a man of principle and intended to appoint him chancellor.

sentences.zh: 趙普忌儀剛直，乃引薛居正參知政事。

translations.literal: Zhao Pu resented Yi's blunt uprightness and instead brought in Xue Juzheng as Deputy Director of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu, resenting Yi's uncompromising honesty, instead brought Xue Juzheng in as Deputy Director of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及儀卒，太祖憫然謂左右曰：「天何奪我竇儀之速耶！」

translations.literal: When Yi died, Taizu said mournfully to those beside him, "Why does Heaven take my Dou Yi so quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died, Taizu said sadly to those around him, "Why does Heaven take Dou Yi from me so soon!"

sentences.zh: 蓋惜其未大用也。

translations.literal: It was because he regretted that Yi had never been fully employed.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved that Yi had never been given his full measure of use.

sentences.zh: 侃，漢乾佑初及第，至起居郎。

translations.literal: Kan passed the examination in the early Gan-you era of Han and rose to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Kan passed the examination early in the Han dynasty's Gan-you era and rose as far as Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 僖，周廣順初及第，至左補闕。

translations.literal: Xi passed the examination in the early Guang-shun era of Zhou and rose to Left Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xi passed in the early Zhou reign of Guang-shun and rose to Left Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 子諲、諹、誥，俱登進士第，諲至都官員外郎，諹至秘書丞。

translations.literal: His sons Shen, Yong, and Gao all attained the jinshi degree; Shen rose to Vice Director in the Bureau of Capital Administration, and Yong to Secretary Aide.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shen, Yong, and Gao all passed the jinshi examination; Shen rose to Vice Director in the Bureau of Capital Administration, and Yong to Secretary Aide.

sentences.zh: 弟 儼

translations.literal: Younger brother Yan
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother: Yan

sentences.zh: 儼，字望之，幼能屬文。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Wangzhi, could compose prose while still young.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Wangzhi, could already write polished prose in boyhood.

sentences.zh: 既冠，舉晉天福六年進士，辟滑州從事。

translations.literal: After coming of age he passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Tianfu of Jin and was recruited as an aide in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching adulthood he passed the jinshi examination in Jin's sixth year of Tianfu and was appointed an aide in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 府罷，授著作佐郎、集賢校理，出為天平軍掌書記，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: When the prefectural office was abolished, he was appointed Assistant Editor and collator in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, then went out as secretary to the Tianping Army; he left office to observe mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When that prefectural post was abolished, he was made Assistant Editor and collator in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, then served as secretary to the Tianping Army before resigning to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed Left Remonstrance and Memorial Writer.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed Left Remonstrance and Memorial Writer.

sentences.zh: 開運中，諸鎮恣用酷刑，儼上疏曰：「案名例律，死刑二，絞、斬之謂也。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyun era, the various military prefectures used cruel punishments at will. Yan submitted a memorial saying, "According to the statutes on nomenclature and precedent, there are two capital punishments: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun era, regional commanders freely inflicted cruel punishments. Yan submitted a memorial: "Under the statutes of nomenclature and precedent, there are only two capital punishments: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 絞者筋骨相連，斬者頭頸異處，大辟之目，不出兩端。

translations.literal: In strangulation sinew and bone remain joined; in decapitation head and neck lie apart. The categories of supreme penalty go no further than these two.
translations.idiomatic: Strangulation leaves sinew and bone still joined; decapitation separates head from neck. The supreme punishments extend no further than these two forms.

sentences.zh: 淫刑之興，近聞數等，蓋緣外地不守通規，或以長釘貫人手足，或以短刀臠人肌膚，遷延信宿，不令就死。

translations.literal: The rise of excessive punishments—I have lately heard of several kinds—comes mostly because outer regions do not observe the common rules, sometimes driving long nails through a person's hands and feet, sometimes slicing flesh with short blades, prolonging the agony over nights without allowing death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have lately heard of several kinds of excessive punishment, mostly because distant regions ignore the standard code—driving long nails through hands and feet, or carving flesh with short knives, dragging out the torment over days and nights without permitting death.

sentences.zh: 冤聲上達，和氣有傷，望加禁止。」

translations.literal: Cries of injustice reach on high, and the harmony of qi is harmed. I hope this may be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: The cries of the wronged rise to Heaven, and the world's harmonious qi is wounded. I beg that such practices be forbidden."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his request.

sentences.zh: 儼仕漢為史館修撰。

translations.literal: Yan served the Han dynasty as historiographer in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han, Yan served as historiographer in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，遷右補闕，與賈緯、王伸同修晉高祖、少帝、漢祖三朝實錄。

translations.literal: In the early Guang-shun era of Zhou he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor and, together with Jia Wei and Wang Shen, compiled the Veritable Records of the three reigns of Jin Gaozu, Jin Shaodi, and the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou reign of Guang-shun he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor and, with Jia Wei and Wang Shen, compiled the Veritable Records of Jin Gaozu, Jin Shaodi, and the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 改主客員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Receiving Guests and put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Vice Director in the Bureau of Receiving Guests and charged with drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 時儀自閤下入翰林，兄弟同日拜命，分居兩制，時人榮之。

translations.literal: At that time Yi entered the Hanlin Academy from the Secretariat gate; the brothers received appointments on the same day and were placed in the two drafting bureaus, to the admiration of their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yi entered the Hanlin Academy from the inner secretariat, and the brothers were appointed on the same day to the two drafting offices—a distinction their contemporaries greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 俄加金部郎中，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was additionally made Vice Director in the Bureau of Gold and appointed Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was further made Vice Director in the Bureau of Gold and appointed Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，加集賢殿學士，判院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande he was additionally made Academician of the Jixian Hall and placed in charge of the institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiande he was additionally made Academician of the Jixian Hall and placed in charge of the institute.

sentences.zh: 父憂去職，服闋，復舊官。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's death; when mourning ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on his father's death; when mourning ended he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 時世宗方切於治道，儼上疏曰：「曆代致理，六綱為首：一曰明禮，禮不明則彝倫不敘。

translations.literal: At the time Shizong was keenly devoted to the way of governance, and Yan submitted a memorial saying, "Throughout the ages, bringing order to the realm begins with six guiding principles. The first is clarifying ritual: if ritual is unclear, human relations lack proper order.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shizong was keenly devoted to governing well, and Yan submitted a memorial: "Throughout the ages, bringing order to the realm begins with six guiding principles. The first is clarifying ritual: if ritual is unclear, human relations lack proper order.

sentences.zh: 二曰崇樂，樂不崇則二儀不和。

translations.literal: The second is honoring music: if music is not honored, heaven and earth are not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The second is honoring music: if music is not honored, heaven and earth are not in harmony.

sentences.zh: 三曰熙政，政不熙則群務不整。

translations.literal: The third is illuminating government: if government is not illuminated, the multitude of affairs are not put in order.
translations.idiomatic: The third is illuminating government: if government is not illuminated, public affairs are not put in order.

sentences.zh: 四曰正刑，刑不正則巨奸不懾。

translations.literal: The fourth is rectifying punishments: if punishments are not rectified, great villains are not awed.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth is rectifying punishments: if punishments are not rectified, great villains are not awed.

sentences.zh: 五曰勸農，農不勸則資澤不流。

translations.literal: The fifth is encouraging agriculture: if agriculture is not encouraged, resources and bounty do not flow.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth is encouraging agriculture: if agriculture is not encouraged, resources and bounty do not flow.

sentences.zh: 六曰經武，武不經則軍功不盛。

translations.literal: The sixth is regulating military affairs: if military affairs are not regulated, martial achievement does not flourish.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth is regulating military affairs: if military affairs are not regulated, martial achievement does not flourish.

sentences.zh: 故禮有紀，若人之衣冠；

translations.literal: Thus ritual has its standards, like a person's robes and cap;
translations.idiomatic: Thus ritual has its standards, like a person's robes and cap;

sentences.zh: 樂有章，若人之喉舌；

translations.literal: music has its patterns, like a person's throat and tongue;
translations.idiomatic: music has its patterns, like a person's throat and tongue;

sentences.zh: 政有統，若人之情性；

translations.literal: government has its governing principle, like a person's disposition;
translations.idiomatic: government has its governing principle, like a person's disposition;

sentences.zh: 刑有制，若人之呼吸；

translations.literal: punishments have their regulations, like a person's breathing;
translations.idiomatic: punishments have their regulations, like a person's breathing;

sentences.zh: 農為本，若人之飲食；

translations.literal: agriculture is the root, like a person's food and drink;
translations.idiomatic: agriculture is the root, like a person's food and drink;

sentences.zh: 武為用，若人之手足。

translations.literal: and military affairs are the instrument, like a person's hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: and military affairs are the instrument, like a person's hands and feet.

sentences.zh: 斯六者，不可斯須而去身也。

translations.literal: These six cannot for an instant be separated from the person.
translations.idiomatic: These six cannot for an instant be separated from the person.

sentences.zh: 陛下思服帝猷，寤寐獻納，亟下方正之詔，廓開藝能之路。

translations.literal: Your Majesty thinks on the emperor's design, seeks counsel waking and sleeping, urgently issues edicts for upright men, and opens wide the path of talent and skill.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reflects on the emperor's design, seeks counsel waking and sleeping, urgently issues edicts for upright men, and opens wide the path of talent and skill.

sentences.zh: 士有一技，必得自效。

translations.literal: When a scholar has one skill, he is sure to be able to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: When a scholar has one skill, he is sure to be able to offer his service.

sentences.zh: 故小臣不揆，輒陳禮、樂、刑、政、勸農、經武之言。」

translations.literal: Therefore this humble subject, without measuring his place, ventures to set forth words on ritual, music, punishments, government, encouraging agriculture, and regulating military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore this humble subject, without measuring his place, ventures to set forth words on ritual, music, punishments, government, encouraging agriculture, and regulating military affairs."

sentences.zh: 世宗多見聽納。

translations.literal: Shizong largely accepted and acted on it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong largely accepted and acted on it.

sentences.zh: 南征還。

translations.literal: He returned from the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He returned from the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 詔儼考正雅樂，俄權知貢舉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yan to examine and rectify the court music; soon afterward he served as acting supervisor of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Yan to examine and correct the court music, and soon afterward he served as acting supervisor of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜翰林學士，判太常寺。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Hanlin Academician and given concurrent charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was appointed Hanlin Academician and given concurrent charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 儼校鍾磬筦龠之數，辨清濁上下之節，復舉律呂旋相為宮之法，迄今遵用。

translations.literal: Yan corrected the numbers of bells, chime-stones, pipes, and flutes, distinguished the intervals of clear and muddy, high and low pitch, and revived the method by which the pitch-pipes cyclically generate the modes—a method still followed to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Yan corrected the tuning of bells, chime-stones, pipes, and flutes, clarified the distinctions of clear and muddy pitch and of upper and lower registers, and restored the method by which the twelve pitch-pipes cyclically generate the modes—a system still followed in his day.

sentences.zh: 會詔中外臣僚，有所聞見，並許上章論議。

translations.literal: An edict then summoned officials throughout the court and the provinces: all who had observations were permitted to submit memorials for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then invited officials throughout the court and the provinces to submit memorials on whatever they had observed or concluded.

sentences.zh: 儼疏曰：「設官分職，授政任功，欲為政之有倫，在位官之無曠。

translations.literal: Yan submitted a memorial saying, "Offices are established and duties divided; governance is entrusted and merit assigned—the aim is that government have order and that no post stand vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted a memorial: "Offices are established and duties divided; power is delegated and achievement rewarded—the purpose is an ordered government and no idle post in the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷多士，省寺華資，無事有員，十乃六七，止於計月待奉，計年待遷。

translations.literal: Now the court has many scholars, yet in the prestigious posts of the ministries and directorates, six or seven out of ten officeholders have nothing to do; they merely count the months for their salaries and the years until promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Today the court is full of educated men, yet in the ministries and directorates six or seven out of ten holders of fine-sounding posts have nothing to do—they merely count months for their stipends and years until promotion.

sentences.zh: 其中廉幹之人，不無愧恥之意。

translations.literal: Among them, the honest and capable must feel shame.
translations.idiomatic: Even the honest and capable among them must feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 如非歷試，何展公才。

translations.literal: If they are not tested through actual service, how can public talent be displayed?
translations.idiomatic: Without real trials of service, how can public talent ever be brought forth?

sentences.zh: 請改兩畿諸縣令及外州府五千戶以上縣令為縣大夫，升為從五品下。

translations.literal: I request that magistrates of counties in the two capitals, and magistrates of counties with more than five thousand households in outer prefectures, be renamed County Grandees and raised to the lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that magistrates of counties in the two metropolitan circuits, and of counties with more than five thousand households elsewhere, be renamed County Grandees and raised to lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 畿大夫見府尹如赤令之儀，其諸州府縣大夫見本部長如賓從之禮。

translations.literal: Grand masters in the capital circuit would meet the prefect with the ceremony due a magistrate in red robes; grandees in other prefectures would meet their superiors with the courtesy due host and guest.
translations.idiomatic: Capital grandees would meet the prefect with the ceremony owed a chief magistrate; provincial grandees would meet their superiors with the formal courtesy of host and guest.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎、起居、補闕、拾遺、侍御史、殿中侍御史、監察御史、光祿少卿以下四品，太常丞以下五品等，並得衣朱紫。

translations.literal: Directors, vice directors, attendants, remonstrance censors, memorial writers, attending censors, palace censors, and investigatory censors, together with the Vice Minister of Imperial Household and all offices below the fourth rank, and the Director of Ceremonies and all offices below the fifth rank, would all be permitted to wear red and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Directors, vice directors, attendants, remonstrance censors, memorial writers, attending censors, palace censors, and investigatory censors, together with the Vice Minister of Imperial Household and all posts of fourth rank and below, and the Director of Ceremonies and all posts of fifth rank and below, would all be allowed to wear red and purple.

sentences.zh: 滿日，準在朝一任，約舊官遷二等。

translations.literal: When their term was complete, it would count as one stint at court, and they would be promoted roughly two ranks above their former office.
translations.idiomatic: On completing their term, they would count it as one full stint at court and be promoted roughly two ranks above their former office.

sentences.zh: 自拾遺、監察除授回日，即為起居、侍御史、中行員外郎。

translations.literal: From the day of appointment after service as remonstrance or investigatory censor, they would become attendants, attending censors, or middle-rank vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: From the day they returned after appointment from remonstrance or investigatory posts, they would advance to attendant, attending censor, or middle-rank vice director.

sentences.zh: 若前官不是三署，即罷後一年方得求仕。

translations.literal: If their previous office was not one of the Three Bureaus, they would have to wait one year after dismissal before seeking office again.
translations.idiomatic: If their previous post had not been in one of the Three Bureaus, they would have to wait a full year after leaving office before seeking appointment again.

sentences.zh: 如此，則士大夫足以陳力，賢不肖無以駕肩，各係否臧，明行黜陟，利民益國，斯實良規。」

translations.literal: In this way the scholar-officials would be able to exert their strength fully; the worthy and unworthy could not stand shoulder to shoulder; each would be tied to merit or failure; promotion and demotion would be made clear; the people would benefit and the state would gain—truly a sound plan."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the scholar-officials could truly exert themselves; worthy and unworthy men could no longer stand shoulder to shoulder; each would rise or fall by his own merit; promotion and demotion would be plain; the people would benefit and the state would gain. This would be a sound policy indeed."

sentences.zh: 又以為：「家國之方，守穀帛而已，二者不出國而出於民。

translations.literal: He also argued: "The foundation of house and state lies merely in guarding grain and silk; these two do not come from the state but from the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The foundation of family and state is simply the safeguarding of grain and silk. Neither comes from the treasury; both come from the people.

sentences.zh: 其道在天，其利在地，得其理者蕃阜，失其理者耗嗇。

translations.literal: Their way lies in Heaven, their profit in the earth; grasp the principle and abundance follows, lose it and want sets in.
translations.idiomatic: Their course depends on Heaven, their yield on the land. Where the principle is understood, plenty flourishes; where it is lost, scarcity and stinginess follow.

sentences.zh: 民之顓蒙，宜有勸教。

translations.literal: The people's dullness calls for encouragement and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The people are simple and uninstructed; they need encouragement and teaching.

sentences.zh: 請於《齊民要術》及《四時纂要》、《韋氏月錄》中，采其關於田蠶園囿之事，集為一卷，鏤板頒行，使之流布。」

translations.literal: I request that passages concerning farming, sericulture, gardens, and orchards be selected from Essential Arts for the Common People, the Seasonal Compendium, and the Wei Clan Monthly Record, compiled into one volume, carved on blocks, and issued so that it may circulate widely."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that passages on farming, sericulture, gardens, and orchards be gathered from Essential Arts for the Common People, the Seasonal Compendium, and the Wei Clan Monthly Record, compiled into one volume, printed, and distributed widely."

sentences.zh: 疏奏不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no answer came.

sentences.zh: 宋初，就轉禮部侍郎，代儀知貢舉。

translations.literal: Early in the Song dynasty he was transferred directly to Vice Minister of Rites and replaced Yi as supervisor of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was transferred directly to Vice Minister of Rites and took over from Yi as supervisor of the examinations.

sentences.zh: 當是時，祀事樂章、宗廟諡號多儼撰定，議者服其該博。

translations.literal: At that time the hymns for sacrificial rites and the posthumous titles for the imperial temples were largely drafted by Yan, and commentators admired his comprehensive learning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many of the sacrificial hymns and temple posthumous titles were drafted by Yan, and critics admired the breadth of his learning.

sentences.zh: 車駕征澤、潞，以疾不從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against Ze and Lu, he did not accompany it because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor marched against Ze and Lu, Yan did not accompany the campaign because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 儼性夷曠，好賢樂善，優遊策府凡十餘年。

translations.literal: Yan was easygoing and broad-minded, loved the worthy and delighted in good deeds, and spent more than ten years at ease in the Academy archives.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was open and unhurried in temperament, loved worthies and delighted in good deeds, and passed more than ten leisurely years in the Academy archives.

sentences.zh: 所撰《周正樂》成一百二十卷，詔藏於史閣；

translations.literal: The Correct Music of Zhou that he compiled reached one hundred and twenty volumes, and an edict ordered it stored in the historiography pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His Correct Music of Zhou, completed in one hundred and twenty volumes, was ordered stored in the historiography pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其《通禮》未及編纂而卒。

translations.literal: His Comprehensive Rites he did not live to compile.
translations.idiomatic: His Comprehensive Rites he did not live to finish.

sentences.zh: 有文集七十卷。

translations.literal: He left collected writings in seventy volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in seventy volumes.

sentences.zh: 儼與儀尤為才俊，對景覽古，皆形諷詠，更迭倡和至二百篇，多以道義相敦勵，並著集。

translations.literal: Yan and Yi were especially talented; viewing scenes and antiquities, they both composed poetry in response, alternating in mutual composition to two hundred pieces, mostly encouraging one another in righteousness; both published collections.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Yi were especially gifted. Contemplating landscapes and antiquities, each turned what he saw into verse; they exchanged poems back and forth until they had more than two hundred pieces, mostly urging one another toward duty and integrity. Both left published collections.

sentences.zh: 儼顯德中奉使荊南。

translations.literal: During the Xiande era Yan served as envoy to Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era Yan went on mission to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 荊南自唐季以來，高氏據有其地，雖名藩臣，車服多僭侈逾制，以至司賓賤隸、候館小胥，皆盛服彯纓，與王人亢禮。

translations.literal: Since the late Tang, the Gao clan had held that region. Though nominally a vassal domain, its carriages and robes often exceeded protocol in extravagance, so that even guest officers, low attendants, and hostel clerks wore splendid dress with tasseled caps and claimed equal standing with the Emperor's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Since late Tang the Gao clan had held Jingnan. Though nominally a vassal state, its carriages and robes often exceeded proper rank in lavish display—even guest officers, low attendants, and inn clerks wore splendid dress with tasseled caps and treated themselves as equals of the Emperor's envoys.

sentences.zh: 儼諷以天子在上，諸侯當各守法度，悉令去之，然後宣達君命。

translations.literal: Yan subtly admonished them that with the Son of Heaven above, the feudal lords ought each to keep to law and measure; he ordered all such excess removed, and only then proclaimed the sovereign's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yan gently reminded them that with the Son of Heaven above, every lord should keep to his proper measure. He had all such excess stripped away, and only then delivered the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 尤善推步星曆，逆知吉凶。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at calendrical astronomy and could foreknow fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in calendrical astronomy and could foretell fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 盧多遜、楊徽之同任諫官，儼嘗謂之曰：「丁卯歲五星聚奎，自此天下太平，二拾遺見之，儼不與也。」

translations.literal: Lu Duoxun and Yang Huizhi both served as remonstrance officials. Yan once told them, "In the dingmao year the five planets will gather at Kui; from then on all under Heaven will be at peace. You two remonstrance officials will see it—I shall not."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duoxun and Yang Huizhi were serving together as remonstrance officials when Yan told them, "In the dingmao year the five planets will gather at the Kui asterism, and from then peace will reign under Heaven. You two remonstrance officials will live to see it—I shall not."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「儼家昆弟五人，皆登進士第，可謂盛矣，然無及相輔者，唯偁稍近之，亦不久居其位。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Five brothers in Yan's house have all passed the jinshi examination—splendid indeed. Yet none will reach the rank of assisting the throne; only Cheng comes close, and even he will not long hold that post."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The five brothers of our house have all passed the jinshi examination—a great honor. Yet none will rise to chancellor; only Cheng will come close, and even he will not long keep the post."

sentences.zh: 卒如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it happened exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end everything happened just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 儼有子早卒，以侄說為嗣。

translations.literal: Yan's son died young, and he made his nephew Shuo his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son died young, so he adopted his nephew Shuo as heir.

sentences.zh: 弟 偁

translations.literal: Younger brother Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother: Cheng

sentences.zh: 偁，字日章，漢乾祐二年舉進士。

translations.literal: Cheng, courtesy name Rizhang, passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Gan-you of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, styled Rizhang, passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Han reign of Gan-you.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，補單州軍事判官，遷秘書郎，出為絳州防禦判官。

translations.literal: In the early Guang-shun era of Zhou he was appointed military judge of Shan Prefecture, then promoted to Secretary, and later sent out as defense judge of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou reign of Guang-shun he was made military judge of Shan Prefecture, promoted to Secretary, and later sent out as defense judge of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋初，歷武寧軍掌書記西京留守判官、天雄歸德軍節度判官。

translations.literal: Early in the Song dynasty he successively served as secretary to the Wuning Army, judge to the Western Capital garrison commander, and judge to the military commissioner of the Tianxiong and Guide armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served in succession as secretary to the Wuning Army, judge to the Western Capital garrison commander, and judge on the staff of the Tianxiong-Guide military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，拜右補闕、知宋州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he was appointed Right Remonstrance Censor and made prefect of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he was appointed Right Remonstrance Censor and put in charge of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《遂命賦》以自悼。

translations.literal: He once wrote the rhapsody "Following Fate" to lament his own lot.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a rhapsody called "Following Fate" to mourn his own fortunes.

sentences.zh: 太宗領開封尹，選偁判官。

translations.literal: When Taizong held the post of Prefect of Kaifeng, he chose Cheng as his judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong served as Prefect of Kaifeng, he selected Cheng as his administrative judge.

sentences.zh: 時賈琰為推官，偁不樂其為人。

translations.literal: At the time Jia Yan served as investigating officer, and Cheng disliked his character.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jia Yan was the investigating officer, and Cheng took no pleasure in the man.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗宴諸王，偁、琰與會，琰言矯誕，偁叱之曰：「巧言令色，心不獨愧乎。」

translations.literal: Taizong once gave a feast for the princes; Cheng and Yan were present. Yan spoke in forced and extravagant terms, and Cheng rebuked him, saying, "Fair words and a pleasing face—does your heart not feel ashamed by itself?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once feasted the princes, with Cheng and Yan in attendance. Yan spoke in florid and exaggerated tones, and Cheng rebuked him: "Fine words and a pleasing face—does your heart feel no shame of its own?"

sentences.zh: 上愕然，因罷會，出偁為彰義軍節度判官。

translations.literal: The Emperor was startled, broke off the feast, and sent Cheng out as judge on the staff of the Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was startled, cut the feast short, and sent Cheng out as judge on the staff of the Zhangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，車駕幸大名府，召至行在所，拜比部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, when the imperial carriage visited Daming Prefecture, Cheng was summoned to the traveling palace and appointed Director in the Bureau of Finance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, when the Emperor visited Daming Prefecture, Cheng was summoned to the traveling palace and appointed Director in the Bureau of Finance.

sentences.zh: 時議北征，偁請休兵牧馬，以徐圖之，上從其言。

translations.literal: When a northern campaign was under discussion, Cheng urged resting the troops and grazing the horses, planning the matter slowly; the Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: When a northern campaign was debated, Cheng urged resting the army and grazing the horses, taking a slower course toward victory, and the Emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 歸，以偁為樞密直學士，賜第一區。

translations.literal: On returning, he made Cheng a Privy Council academician and granted him one prime residence.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, he made Cheng a Privy Council academician and granted him a first-rank residence.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷左諫議大夫，充職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee and continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee and continued in office.

sentences.zh: 七年，參知政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he became Deputy Director of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made Deputy Director of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上謂偁曰：「汝何能臻此？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Cheng, "How did you reach this position?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Cheng, "How did you come to this?"

sentences.zh: 偁曰：「陛下不忘舊臣。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Your Majesty has not forgotten an old servant."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty has not forgotten an old servant."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「非也，卿能以公正責賈琰，朕旌直臣爾。」

translations.literal: Taizong said, "Not so. You were able, with impartial justice, to rebuke Jia Yan; I am simply honoring an upright minister."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "No. You had the courage to rebuke Jia Yan with impartial justice. I am simply rewarding an upright minister—that is all."

sentences.zh: 是秋卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died that autumn at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died that autumn at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨哭，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage attended his mourning, and he was posthumously awarded the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came in person to mourn him and posthumously ennobled him as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，偁在涇州，與丁顥同官，顥子謂方幼，偁見之曰：「此兒必遠到。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cheng was in Jing Prefecture serving with Ding Hao, Hao's son Wei was still young. Cheng saw him and said, "This boy will go far."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Cheng was serving in Jing Prefecture alongside Ding Hao, Hao's son Wei was still a boy. Cheng saw him and said, "This child will go far."

sentences.zh: 以女妻之。

translations.literal: He gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 後為宰相、三公。

translations.literal: Later he served as Grand Chancellor and one of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Grand Chancellor and one of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂宰相曰：「近朝卿士，竇儀質重嚴整，有家法，閨門敦睦，人無讕語，諸弟不能及。

translations.literal: Taizu once said to the chief ministers: "Among recent court officials, Dou Yi is grave, dignified, and orderly; he maintains household regulations; harmony reigns within his gates; no one speaks ill of him—his younger brothers cannot match him. Xi is also of middling talent, but Cheng is said to have integrity and high principles, which is commendable.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once told the chief ministers: "Among recent court officials, Dou Yi is grave, dignified, and orderly; he keeps strict household rules; harmony reigns within his gates; no one speaks ill of him—none of his younger brothers can match him. Xi is also of middling talent, but Cheng is said to have integrity and high principles, which is commendable.

sentences.zh: 僖亦中人材爾，偁有操尚，可嘉也。」

translations.literal: Xi is also of middling talent, but Cheng is said to have integrity and high principles, which is commendable."
translations.idiomatic: Xi is only of middling talent, but Cheng is said to have integrity and high principles, which is commendable."

sentences.zh: 呂餘慶

translations.literal: Lu Yuqing
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuqing

sentences.zh: 呂餘慶，幽州安次人，本名胤，犯太祖偏諱，因以字行。

translations.literal: Lu Yuqing, a native of Anci in Youzhou, was originally named Yin; because this violated a partial taboo of Taizu's name, he went by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuqing, a native of Anci in Youzhou, was originally named Yin; because this violated a partial taboo of Taizu's name, he went by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 祖兗，橫海軍節度判官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan served as administrative aide to the military governor of the Henghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan served as administrative aide to the military governor of the Henghai Army.

sentences.zh: 父琦，晉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Qi was Vice Minister of Personnel under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi served as Vice Minister of Personnel under Jin.

sentences.zh: 餘慶以蔭補千牛備身，歷開封府參軍，遷戶曹掾。

translations.literal: Yuqing entered office through yin privilege as a Palace Guard attendant, served as aide in Kaifeng Prefecture, and was promoted to bureau assistant in the Households Section.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing entered office through yin privilege as a Palace Guard attendant, served as an aide in Kaifeng Prefecture, and was promoted to bureau assistant in the Households Section.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝弟重睿領忠武軍節度，以餘慶為推官。

translations.literal: When Chong Rui, younger brother of Jin's Emperor Shaodi, held the military governorship of the Zhongwu Army, Yuqing was made push officer on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong Rui, the younger brother of Jin's Emperor Shaodi, held the military governorship of the Zhongwu Army, Yuqing was made push officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 仕漢歷周，遷濮州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Serving through Han and into Zhou, he was promoted to recording aide in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Serving through Han and into Zhou, he was promoted to recording aide in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖領同州節制，聞餘慶有材，奏為從事。

translations.literal: When Taizu held military governorship of Tong Prefecture, hearing that Yuqing had talent, he memorialized to appoint him staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu held the military governorship of Tong Prefecture and heard that Yuqing had talent, he memorialized to appoint him a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 世宗問曰：「得非嘗為濮州糾曹者乎？」

translations.literal: Shizong asked, "Might this not be the man who once served as investigating clerk in Puzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong asked, "Is this not the man who once served as investigating clerk in Puzhou?"

sentences.zh: 即以為定國軍掌書記。

translations.literal: He then appointed him chief secretary of the Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed him chief secretary of the Dingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗鎮澶淵，濮為屬郡，故知其為人也。

translations.literal: Shizong had once governed at Chanyuan; Pu was a subordinate prefecture, so he already knew the man.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had once governed at Chanyuan, and since Pu was a subordinate prefecture, he already knew the man.

sentences.zh: 太祖歷滑、許、宋三鎮，餘慶並為賓佐。

translations.literal: Taizu successively held the three commands of Hua, Xu, and Song, and Yuqing served on his staff throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu successively held the three commands of Hua, Xu, and Song, and Yuqing served on his staff throughout.

sentences.zh: 及即位，自宋、亳觀察判官召拜給事中，充端明殿學士。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Yuqing was summoned from administrative aide of the Song and Bo observation commission and appointed Giving Affairs Attendant, serving as Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Yuqing was summoned from administrative aide of the Song and Bo observation commission and appointed Giving Affairs Attendant and Academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，琦亦居是職，官秩皆同，時人榮之。

translations.literal: In the Qingtai era Qi also held that post; their offices and ranks were the same, and contemporaries honored them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingtai era his father Qi also held that post; their offices and ranks were the same, and contemporaries honored them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知開封府。

translations.literal: Before long he governed Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he governed Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖征潞及揚，並領上都副留守。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Lu and Yang, Yuqing concurrently served as deputy capital guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned against Lu and Yang, Yuqing concurrently served as deputy capital guardian.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 荊湖平，出知潭州，改襄州，遷兵部侍郎、知江陵府。

translations.literal: When Jinghu was pacified he was sent out to govern Tan Prefecture, then transferred to Xiang Prefecture, promoted to Vice Minister of War, and made prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinghu was pacified he was sent out to govern Tan Prefecture, then transferred to Xiang Prefecture, promoted to Vice Minister of War, and made prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 召還，以本官參知政事。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he became Co-Equal Participant in Governance in his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became Co-Equal Participant in Governance in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，命知成都府。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was ordered to govern Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, he was ordered to govern Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊四起，軍士恃功驕恣，大將王全斌等不能戢下。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere; soldiers, relying on their achievements, grew arrogant and unbridled, and the generals Wang Quanbin and others could not restrain their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits rose everywhere; soldiers, relying on their achievements, grew arrogant and unbridled, and the generals Wang Quanbin and others could not restrain their subordinates.

sentences.zh: 一日，藥市始集，街吏馳報有軍校被酒持刃奪賈人物。

translations.literal: One day, as the medicine market was just opening, a street clerk rushed to report that a military officer, drunk, was wielding a blade and seizing merchants' goods.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as the medicine market was just opening, a street clerk rushed to report that a military officer, drunk and wielding a blade, was seizing merchants' goods.

sentences.zh: 餘慶立捕斬之以徇，軍中畏伏，民用按堵。

translations.literal: Yuqing at once had him seized and executed as a public warning; the army feared and submitted, and the people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing at once had him seized and executed as a public warning; the army feared and submitted, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 就加吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon additionally appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，兼劍南、荊南等道都提舉、三司水陸發運等使。

translations.literal: On returning to court, he also held the posts of overall commissioner for the Jiannan, Jingnan, and other circuits, and commissioner for the Three Departments' land and water transport.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, he also served as overall commissioner for the Jiannan, Jingnan, and other circuits, and as commissioner for the Three Departments' land and water transport.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，與宰相更知政事印，旋以疾上表求解機務，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao, he alternated with the Grand Chancellor in holding the seal of state affairs; shortly afterward he submitted a memorial citing illness to request release from urgent duties and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he alternated with the Grand Chancellor in holding the seal of state affairs; shortly afterward he submitted a memorial citing illness to request release from urgent duties and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年五十。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died at fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮南軍節度。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as military governor of the Zhennan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as military governor of the Zhennan Army.

sentences.zh: 餘慶重厚簡易，自太祖繼領藩鎮，餘慶為元僚。

translations.literal: Yuqing was steady, grave, and unpretentious; from the time Taizu successively held frontier commands, Yuqing was his chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing was steady, grave, and unpretentious; from the time Taizu successively held frontier commands, Yuqing was his chief aide.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，趙普、李處耘皆先進用，餘慶恬不為意。

translations.literal: When the throne was received, Zhao Pu and Li Chuyun were both promoted first; Yuqing was calmly unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was received, Zhao Pu and Li Chuyun were both promoted first, but Yuqing remained calmly unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，處耘黜守淄州，餘慶自江陵還，太祖委曲問處耘事，餘慶以理辨釋，上以為實，遂命參知政事。

translations.literal: Before long Chuyun was demoted to govern Zizhou; Yuqing returned from Jiangling. Taizu questioned him in detail about Chuyun's affair. Yuqing explained it on rational grounds; the Emperor considered it true and thereupon appointed him Deputy Director of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chuyun was demoted to govern Zizhou. Yuqing returned from Jiangling, and Taizu questioned him in detail about Chuyun's affair. Yuqing explained it on rational grounds; the Emperor found his account credible and thereupon appointed him Deputy Director of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會趙普忤旨，左右爭傾普，餘慶獨辨明之，太祖意稍解，時稱其長者。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pu ran afoul of the imperial will, those at court vied to bring him down, but Yuqing alone spoke in his defense. Taizu's mind eased somewhat, and contemporaries praised him as a man of mature judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pu ran afoul of the imperial will, those at court vied to bring him down, but Yuqing alone spoke in his defense. Taizu's mind eased somewhat, and contemporaries praised him as a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 至道中，以弟端為宰相，特詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era, because his younger brother Duan became Grand Chancellor, he was specially enfeoffed by edict as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhidao era, because his younger brother Duan became Grand Chancellor, he was specially enfeoffed by edict as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉熙古

translations.literal: Liu Xigu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xigu

sentences.zh: 劉熙古，字義淳，宋州寧陵人，唐左僕射仁軌十一世孫。

translations.literal: Liu Xigu, styled Yichun, was a native of Ningling in Songzhou and eleventh-generation descendant of Tang's Left Vice Director Ren'gui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xigu, courtesy name Yichun, was a native of Ningling in Songzhou and an eleventh-generation descendant of Tang's Left Vice Director Ren'gui.

sentences.zh: 祖寶進，嘗為汝陰令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Baojin had once served as magistrate of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Baojin had once served as magistrate of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 熙古年十五，通《易》、《詩》、《書》；

translations.literal: At fifteen Xigu had mastered the Changes, Odes, and Documents;
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Xigu had mastered the Changes, Odes, and Documents;

sentences.zh: 十九，通《春秋》、子、史。

translations.literal: at nineteen he had mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Masters, and histories.
translations.idiomatic: at nineteen he had mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Masters, and histories.

sentences.zh: 避祖諱，不舉進士。

translations.literal: Avoiding his grandfather's taboo name, he did not take the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Avoiding his grandfather's taboo name, he did not take the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興中，以《三傳》舉。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era of Later Tang he was nominated on the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changxing era of Later Tang he was nominated on the Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 時翰林學士和凝掌貢舉，熙古獻《春秋極論》二篇、《演論》三篇，凝甚加賞，召與進士試，擢第，遂館於門下。

translations.literal: At the time Hanlin Academician He Ning oversaw the examinations. Xigu submitted two chapters of "Ultimate Discourse on the Spring and Autumn" and three chapters of "Extended Discourse." Ning greatly admired them, summoned him to take the jinshi examination with the others, and he passed—then took residence in Ning's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hanlin Academician He Ning oversaw the examinations. Xigu submitted two chapters of "Ultimate Discourse on the Spring and Autumn" and three chapters of "Extended Discourse." Ning greatly admired them, summoned him to take the jinshi examination with the others, and he passed—then took residence in Ning's household.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，驍將孫鐸以戰功授金州防禦使，表熙古為從事。

translations.literal: In the Qingtai era the fierce general Sun Duo, for battle merit, was made defense commissioner of Jin Prefecture and memorialized for Xigu to serve as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingtai era the fierce general Sun Duo, for battle merit, was made defense commissioner of Jin Prefecture and memorialized for Xigu to serve as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，鐸移汝州，又辟以隨。

translations.literal: Early in Tianfu under Jin, Duo was transferred to Ru Prefecture, and again recruited Xigu to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin reign of Tianfu, Duo was transferred to Ru Prefecture and again recruited Xigu to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 熙古善騎射，一日，有鶚集戟門槐樹，高八尺，鐸惡之，投以瓦石不去，熙古引弓一發，貫鶚於樹。

translations.literal: Xigu was skilled at horsemanship and archery. One day an osprey alighted on a pagoda-tree at the halberd gate, eight feet high. Duo disliked it and threw tiles and stones, but it would not leave. Xigu drew his bow and in one shot pierced the osprey through to the tree.
translations.idiomatic: Xigu was skilled at horsemanship and archery. One day an osprey alighted on a pagoda-tree at the halberd gate, eight feet high. Duo disliked it and threw tiles and stones, but it would not leave. Xigu drew his bow and in one shot pinned the osprey to the tree.

sentences.zh: 鐸喜，令勿拔矢，以旌其能。

translations.literal: Duo was pleased and ordered that the arrow not be removed, to honor his skill.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was pleased and ordered that the arrow not be removed, to honor his skill.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，鐸卒，調補下邑令。

translations.literal: Two years later Duo died; Xigu was transferred to fill a post as magistrate of a lower county.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Duo died, and Xigu was transferred to fill a post as magistrate of a lower county.

sentences.zh: 俄為三司戶部出使巡官，領永興、渭橋、華州諸倉制置發運。

translations.literal: Shortly he became inspection touring officer of the Three Departments' Households Bureau, overseeing the warehouses and transport arrangements at Yongxing, Weiqiao, Hua Prefecture, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became inspection touring officer of the Three Departments' Households Bureau, overseeing the warehouses and transport arrangements at Yongxing, Weiqiao, Hua Prefecture, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 仕漢，為盧氏令。

translations.literal: Serving Han, he became magistrate of Lu County.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Han, he became magistrate of Lu County.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，改亳州防禦推官，歷澶州支使。

translations.literal: In Guangshun under Zhou he was made push officer of Bozhou defense command, then served as branch commissioner of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou reign of Guangshun he was made push officer of the Bozhou defense command, then served as branch commissioner of Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秦、鳳平，以為秦州觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Qin and Feng were pacified, he was made administrative aide of the Qinzhou observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin and Feng were pacified, he was made administrative aide of the Qinzhou observation commission.

sentences.zh: 太祖領宋州，為節度判官。

translations.literal: When Taizu held Song Prefecture, Xigu served as administrative aide to the military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu held Song Prefecture, Xigu served as administrative aide to the military governor.

sentences.zh: 即位，召為左諫議大夫，知青州。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Xigu was summoned as Left Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee and made prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Xigu was summoned as Left Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee and made prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 車駕征維揚，追赴行在。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against Weiyang, he was summoned to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage campaigned against Weiyang, he was summoned to the temporary palace.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，受詔制置晉州榷礬，增課八十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he received orders to organize the alum monopoly in Jin Prefecture, increasing revenue by more than eight hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he received orders to organize the alum monopoly in Jin Prefecture, increasing revenue by more than eight hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，遷刑部侍郎、知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: Early in Qiande he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments and made prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments and made prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移秦州。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州境所接多寇患，熙古至，諭以朝廷恩信，取蕃部酋豪子弟為質，邊鄙以寧。

translations.literal: The prefecture's borders adjoined many bandit troubles. When Xigu arrived, he instructed them in the court's favor and trust, took sons of tribal chieftains as hostages, and the frontier was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's borders adjoined many bandit troubles. When Xigu arrived, he instructed them in the court's favor and trust, took sons of tribal chieftains as hostages, and the frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部侍郎，徙知成都府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War and moved to govern Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War and moved to govern Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，就拜端明殿學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed on the spot as Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed on the spot as Academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，詔以本官參知政事，選名馬、銀鞍以賜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao an edict made him Co-Equal Participant in Governance in his existing rank and selected famous horses and silver saddles to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao an edict made him Co-Equal Participant in Governance in his existing rank and selected famous horses and silver saddles to bestow on him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以足疾求解，拜戶部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year, citing illness in the foot he requested release and was appointed Minister of Revenue and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, citing illness in the foot he requested release and was appointed Minister of Revenue and retired.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙古兼通陰陽象緯之術，作《續聿斯歌》一卷、《六壬釋卦序例》一卷。

translations.literal: Xigu was also versed in yin-yang, astral omens, and the weft texts; he wrote one scroll of "Continued Yusi Song" and one scroll of "Preface and Examples for Interpreting Hexagrams in the Six Ren."
translations.idiomatic: Xigu was also versed in yin-yang, astral omens, and the weft texts; he wrote one scroll of "Continued Yusi Song" and one scroll of "Preface and Examples for Interpreting Hexagrams in the Six Ren."

sentences.zh: 性淳謹，雖顯貴不改寒素。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and careful; though he rose to high rank he did not change his frugal ways.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was pure and careful; though he rose to high rank he did not change his frugal ways.

sentences.zh: 歷官十八，登朝三十餘年，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: He held eighteen offices and attended court for more than thirty years without ever committing an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He held eighteen offices and attended court for more than thirty years without ever committing an offense.

sentences.zh: 嘗集古今事跡為《歷代紀要》十五卷。

translations.literal: He once compiled events from antiquity to his own time into "Essentials of Successive Ages" in fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled events from antiquity to his own time into "Essentials of Successive Ages" in fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 頗精小學，作《切韻拾玉》二篇，摹刻以獻，詔付國子監頒行之。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled in philology and wrote two chapters of "Gathering Jade from the Cut Rhymes," which he had carved and presented; an edict ordered the Directorate of Education to promulgate it.
translations.idiomatic: He was quite skilled in philology and wrote two chapters of "Gathering Jade from the Cut Rhymes," which he had carved and presented; an edict ordered the Directorate of Education to promulgate it.

sentences.zh: 子蒙正、蒙叟。

translations.literal: His sons were Mengzheng and Mengsou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Mengzheng and Mengsou.

sentences.zh: 子 蒙正

translations.literal: Son Mengzheng
translations.idiomatic: Son: Mengzheng

sentences.zh: 蒙正，字頤正，善騎射。

translations.literal: Mengzheng, styled Yizheng, was skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzheng, courtesy name Yizheng, was skilled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，以蔭補殿直，遷供奉官。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era he entered office through yin privilege as a palace guard, and was promoted to tribute commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiande era he entered office through yin privilege as a palace guard and was promoted to tribute commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王師征江南，命乘傳軍中承奉事。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Jiangnan, he was ordered to travel post-haste in the army on supply and service duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Jiangnan, he was ordered to travel post-haste in the army on supply and service duties.

sentences.zh: 盧絳以舟師來援潤州，蒙正白部署丁德裕，請分精甲百人，出與絳戰，矢中左肋，戰愈力。

translations.literal: Lu Jiang came with a naval force to relieve Runzhou. Mengzheng informed the deployment commander Ding Deyu, asked to take a hundred picked troops to fight Jiang, was struck in the left rib by an arrow, and fought all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiang came with a naval force to relieve Runzhou. Mengzheng informed the deployment commander Ding Deyu, asked to take a hundred picked troops to fight Jiang, was struck in the left rib by an arrow, and fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 及下潤州，獲知州劉澄、監軍崔亮，部送闕下。

translations.literal: When Runzhou fell, they captured Prefect Liu Cheng and army inspector Cui Liang and escorted them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Runzhou fell, they captured Prefect Liu Cheng and army inspector Cui Liang and escorted them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嶺南陸運香藥入京，詔蒙正往規畫。

translations.literal: Fragrant medicinals from Lingnan were transported overland to the capital; Mengzheng was ordered to go and plan the route.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant medicinals from Lingnan were transported overland to the capital, and Mengzheng was ordered to go and plan the route.

sentences.zh: 蒙正請自廣、韶江溯流至南雄；

translations.literal: Mengzheng proposed going up the Guang and Shao rivers to Nanxiong;
translations.idiomatic: Mengzheng proposed going up the Guang and Shao rivers to Nanxiong;

sentences.zh: 由大庾嶺步運至南安軍，凡三鋪，鋪給卒三十人；

translations.literal: then overland by the Dayu Range to Nan'an Army—a total of three relay stations, each staffed with thirty men;
translations.idiomatic: then overland by the Dayu Range to Nan'an Army—a total of three relay stations, each staffed with thirty men;

sentences.zh: 復由水路輸送。

translations.literal: and finally delivery again by water route.
translations.idiomatic: and finally delivery again by water route.

sentences.zh: 又掌朝服法物庫，會重製繡衣、鹵簿，多其規式。

translations.literal: He also managed the court-robes and regalia store; when embroidered robes and imperial escort banners were remade on a large scale, he greatly expanded their specifications.
translations.idiomatic: He also managed the court-robes and regalia store; when embroidered robes and imperial escort banners were remade on a large scale, he greatly expanded their specifications.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，轉內藏庫副使，進崇儀使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Inner Storehouse and promoted to commissioner of the Honored Rites Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Inner Storehouse and promoted to commissioner of the Honored Rites Office.

sentences.zh: 自創內藏庫，即詔蒙正典領，凡二十餘年。

translations.literal: From the founding of the Inner Storehouse he was at once ordered to direct it—for more than twenty years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the Inner Storehouse he was at once ordered to direct it—for more than twenty years in all.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，改如京使，出知滄、冀、磁三州。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenzong's reign he was made palace envoy for capital missions and sent out to govern the three prefectures of Cang, Ji, and Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenzong's reign he was made palace envoy for capital missions and sent out to govern the three prefectures of Cang, Ji, and Ci.

sentences.zh: 戎人犯境，蒙正調丁男乘城固守，有勞。

translations.literal: When border tribes invaded, Mengzheng mobilized adult males to man the walls and hold firm; he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When border tribes invaded, Mengzheng mobilized adult males to man the walls and hold firm, and he earned merit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以擅乘驛馬，責授亳州團練副使。

translations.literal: Before long, for unauthorized use of post horses, he was demoted to deputy training commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for unauthorized use of post horses, he was demoted to deputy training commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子 蒙叟

translations.literal: Son Mengsou
translations.idiomatic: Son: Mengsou

sentences.zh: 蒙叟，字道民，乾德中，進士甲科。

translations.literal: Mengsou, styled Daomin, passed the jinshi examination in the highest category in the Qiande era.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsou, courtesy name Daomin, passed the jinshi examination in the highest category in the Qiande era.

sentences.zh: 歷岳、宿二州推官，以所知論薦，授太子中允、知乾興，拜監察御史，徙知濟州。

translations.literal: He served as push officer in Yue and Su prefectures; through nominations by those who knew him he was appointed Assistant in the Eastern Palace, made prefect of Qianxing, promoted to investigating censor, and transferred to govern Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as push officer in Yue and Su prefectures; through nominations by those who knew him he was appointed Assistant in the Eastern Palace, made prefect of Qianxing, promoted to investigating censor, and transferred to govern Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄以秦王子德恭判州事，就命為通判，郡事皆決於蒙叟。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because Zidegong, Prince of Qin, was assigned to supervise prefectural affairs, Mengsou was at once appointed vice prefect; all prefectural business was decided by Mengsou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, because Zidegong, Prince of Qin, was assigned to supervise prefectural affairs, Mengsou was at once appointed vice prefect, and all prefectural business was decided by Mengsou.

sentences.zh: 遷右補闕，轉起居舍人、戶部鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Officer, then transferred to Diarist of Attendance and Salt-and-Iron Commissioner in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Officer, then transferred to Diarist of Attendance and Salt-and-Iron Commissioner in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 再遷屯田郎中，歷知廬、濠、滁、汝四州，遷都官。

translations.literal: Promoted again to Director in the Bureau of Public Works, he governed in succession Lu, Hao, Chu, and Ru prefectures, and was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again to Director in the Bureau of Public Works, he governed in succession Lu, Hao, Chu, and Ru prefectures, and was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Justice.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，上疏曰：「陛下已周諒闇，方勤萬務，望崇儉德、守前規，無自矜能，無作奢縱，厚三軍之賜，輕萬姓之徭，使化育被於生靈，聲教加於中外。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty has completed the mourning period and now diligently attends to myriad state affairs. I hope you will honor frugal virtue and keep to former regulations: do not pride yourself on your abilities, do not indulge in extravagance and license; enrich the rewards of the Three Armies and lighten the corvée burdens of the myriad people, so that transforming nurture reaches all living beings and imperial instruction extends within and without.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianping era he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty has completed the mourning period and now diligently attends to myriad state affairs. I hope you will honor frugal virtue and keep to former regulations: do not pride yourself on your abilities, do not indulge in extravagance and license; enrich the rewards of the Three Armies and lighten the corvée burdens of the myriad people, so that transforming nurture reaches all living beings and imperial instruction extends within and without.

sentences.zh: 且萬國已觀其始，惟陛下慎守其終，思鮮克之言，戒性習之漸，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the myriad states have already seen the beginning—may Your Majesty carefully guard the end; reflect on the words that few attain completion, and guard against the gradual growth of ingrained habits—then the realm would be greatly blessed."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the myriad states have already seen the beginning—may Your Majesty carefully guard the end; reflect on the words that few attain completion, and guard against the gradual growth of ingrained habits—then the realm would be greatly blessed."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，以本官直史館。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this and, in his current office, made him a compiler in the Historical Archives.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised this and, in his current office, made him a compiler in the Historical Archives.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，令知中宮名。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the north, he was ordered to oversee inner-palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage toured the north, he was ordered to oversee inner-palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 表獻《宋都賦》，述國家受命建號之地，宜建都，立宗廟。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial presenting "Rhapsody on the Song Capital," describing the place where the state received the Mandate and established its name—arguing it should be made the capital and imperial ancestral temples built there.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial presenting "Rhapsody on the Song Capital," describing the place where the state received the Mandate and established its name and arguing that it should be made the capital and imperial ancestral temples built there.

sentences.zh: 時雖未遑，後卒從之。

translations.literal: Though there was no time for this then, the court eventually followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Though there was no time for this then, the court eventually followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 會詔直史館，各獻舊文，以蒙叟所著為嘉，改職方郎中。

translations.literal: When an edict called on those in the Historical Archives to submit former writings, Mengsou's work was judged excellent and he was made Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called on those in the Historical Archives to submit former writings, Mengsou's work was judged excellent and he was made Director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 景德中，以足疾，拜太常少卿致仕。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, because of illness in the feet, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era, because of illness in the feet, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 蒙叟好學，善屬辭，著《五運甲子編年曆》三卷。

translations.literal: Mengsou loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; he wrote "Chronological Calendar of the Five Movements and the Sexagenary Cycle" in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsou loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; he wrote "Chronological Calendar of the Five Movements and the Sexagenary Cycle" in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子宗儒，太子中書；

translations.literal: His son Zongru was Attendant in the Eastern Palace Chancery;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongru was Attendant in the Eastern Palace Chancery;

sentences.zh: 宗弼、宗誨，並進士及第。

translations.literal: Zongbi and Zonghui both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi and Zonghui both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 石熙載，字凝績，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Shi Xizai, styled Ningji, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xizai, courtesy name Ningji, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，進士登第。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era of Zhou he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 疏俊有量，居家嚴謹，有禮法。

translations.literal: Open and talented with breadth of mind, at home he was strict and careful and observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Open and talented with breadth of mind, at home he was strict and careful and observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 宋初，太宗以殿前都虞候領泰寧軍節制，辟為掌書記。

translations.literal: Early in Song, when Taizong held the Taining Army command as Chief Commandant of the Palace Front, he recruited Xizai as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song, when Taizong held the Taining Army command as Chief Commandant of the Palace Front, he recruited Xizai as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 及尹京邑，表為開封府推官。

translations.literal: When Taizong governed the capital district, he recommended Xizai as push officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong governed the capital district, he recommended Xizai as push officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 授右拾遺，遷左補闕。

translations.literal: Xizai was appointed Right Reminder and promoted to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai was appointed Right Reminder and promoted to Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，將起復，以讒出為忠武、崇義二軍掌書記。

translations.literal: On his father's death, when he was about to be recalled from mourning, slander sent him out as chief secretary of the Zhongwu and Chongyi armies.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death, when he was about to be recalled from mourning, slander sent him out as chief secretary of the Zhongwu and Chongyi armies.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，復以左補闕召，同知貢舉。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Xizai was again summoned as Left Supplementation Censor and made co-director of the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Xizai was again summoned as Left Supplementation Censor and made co-director of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 時梅山洞蠻屢為寇，以熙載知潭州。

translations.literal: At the time the Meishan cave tribes repeatedly raided, and Xizai was sent to govern Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Meishan cave tribes repeatedly raided, and Xizai was sent to govern Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召還，擢為兵部員外郎，領樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War and made Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War and made Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，簽書樞密院事，詔賜官第一區。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and an edict granted him a first-rank official residence.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and an edict granted him a first-rank official residence.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，親征河東，以給事中充樞密副使從行，還，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, when the Emperor personally campaigned against Hedong, as Giving Affairs Attendant he served as Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs accompanying the expedition; on return he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, when the Emperor personally campaigned against Hedong, he served as Giving Affairs Attendant and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs accompanying the expedition; on return he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜戶部尚書、樞密使，以病足在告，寢疾久之未愈。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; because of illness in the foot he took leave, and his illness long lingered without cure.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; because of illness in the foot he took leave, and his illness long lingered without cure.

sentences.zh: 八年，上表求解職，詔加慰撫，授尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he submitted a memorial requesting resignation from office; the Emperor issued added consolation and granted him Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he submitted a memorial requesting resignation from office; the Emperor issued added consolation and granted him Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，諡元懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 上為悲歎累日，且謂其事君之心，純正無他，適當委用，而奄忽至此，深為可惜。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned and sighed for many days, saying that Xizai's heart in serving his ruler was pure and single-minded, without other motives; he had been just the man to entrust with employment, yet had suddenly come to this—the loss was deeply regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned and sighed for many days, saying that Xizai's heart in serving his ruler was pure and single-minded, without other motives; he had been just the man to entrust with employment, yet had suddenly come to this—the loss was deeply regrettable.

sentences.zh: 國朝大臣謝事而卒，車駕臨視者，唯熙載焉。

translations.literal: Among great ministers of the dynasty who retired from office and then died, the imperial carriage came in person to pay its respects only in Xizai's case.
