translations.idiomatic: Among great ministers of the dynasty who retired from office and then died, the imperial carriage came in person to pay its respects only in Xizai's case.

sentences.zh: 熙載性忠實，遇事盡言，是非好惡，無所顧避。

translations.literal: Xizai was loyal and honest by nature; in affairs he spoke fully, and in right and wrong, likes and dislikes, he looked to nothing and held back from nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai was loyal and honest by nature; in affairs he spoke fully, and in right and wrong, likes and dislikes, he looked to nothing and held back from nothing.

sentences.zh: 人有善，即推薦之，時論稱其長者。

translations.literal: When others had virtue he at once recommended them; contemporaries praised him as a man of mature judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When others had virtue he at once recommended them; contemporaries praised him as a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 初，遊學時，為養負米。

translations.literal: Early on, while traveling to study, he carried rice on his back to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while traveling to study, he carried rice on his back to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 嘗行嵩陽道中，遇一叟，熟視熙載曰：「真人將興，子當居輔弼之位。」

translations.literal: Once on the road at Songyang he met an old man who looked closely at Xizai and said, "The True Man is about to rise; you will hold the position of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road at Songyang he met an old man who looked closely at Xizai and said, "The True Man is about to rise; you will hold the position of chief minister."

sentences.zh: 言訖不見。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he was seen no more.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking he was seen no more.

sentences.zh: 及居太宗幕下，頗盡誠節。

translations.literal: When he later served under Taizong's command, he fully devoted himself in loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When he later served under Taizong's command, he fully devoted himself in loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 典樞務日，上眷注甚篤，方將倚以為相，俄遘疾不起。

translations.literal: On the days when he directed the Bureau of Military Affairs, the emperor's favor and attention were very deep; he was just about to rely on him as chief minister, when suddenly he fell ill and could not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: While directing the Bureau of Military Affairs, he enjoyed the emperor's deepest trust and was on the verge of being made chief minister, when he suddenly fell gravely ill and never recovered.

sentences.zh: 熙載事繼母牛氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xizai served his stepmother, Lady Niu, and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai was renowned for the filial devotion with which he cared for his stepmother, Lady Niu.

sentences.zh: 弟熙導，牛氏前夫子，隨母歸石氏。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xidao was Lady Niu's son by her previous husband; he followed his mother when she entered the Shi household.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xidao was Lady Niu's son from her previous marriage; he came into the Shi family with his mother.

sentences.zh: 以熙載故，奏補殿直。

translations.literal: Because of Xizai, a memorial was submitted appointing him as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On Xizai's recommendation, he was memorialized for appointment as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從弟熙古、幼弟熙政，皆登進士第，熙載撫之如一。

translations.literal: His cousins Xigu and his youngest brother Xizheng both passed the jinshi examinations; Xizai treated them all alike.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins Xigu and his youngest brother Xizheng both passed the jinshi examinations, and Xizai raised them all with equal care.

sentences.zh: 熙載卒時，子中孚、中立皆幼，熙政患熙導以異姓居己上，乃詐傳上旨，令己籍熙導家財，由是交訟。

translations.literal: When Xizai died, his sons Zhongfu and Zhongli were still young. Xizheng resented that Xidao, of a different surname, stood above him, so he falsely transmitted an imperial order and had the household property of Xidao inventoried; hence mutual lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizai died, his sons Zhongfu and Zhongli were still young. Xizheng resented that Xidao, though of a different surname, outranked him, so he forged an imperial order and had Xidao's family property seized for inventory, sparking a bitter lawsuit between them.

sentences.zh: 有司歸罪熙導，上召問中孚、中立，令有司再鞫得實。

translations.literal: The officials held Xidao responsible. The emperor summoned Zhongfu and Zhongli for questioning and ordered the officials to investigate again until the truth was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities blamed Xidao, but the emperor summoned Zhongfu and Zhongli for questioning and ordered a fresh investigation that uncovered the truth.

sentences.zh: 熙導還本姓，中孚亦養子勿問，熙政坐除名。

translations.literal: Xidao was restored to his original surname; Zhongfu, as an adopted son, was not questioned; Xizheng was punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao was restored to his birth surname; Zhongfu, as an adopted son, was not held accountable; and Xizheng was stripped of his official rank.

sentences.zh: 上素知熙載以母故，育熙導甚厚，雖令還宗，而不奪其官，復以財產量給之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long known that because of his mother, Xizai had raised Xidao very generously. Although he ordered Xidao restored to his original clan, he did not deprive him of his office and again allotted property to him according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long known that Xizai, out of devotion to his mother, had raised Xidao with great generosity. Though he ordered Xidao restored to his birth clan, he did not strip him of his office and allotted him a share of the family property.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年八月，熙載配饗太宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Xianping, Xizai was enshrined for joint sacrifice in Emperor Taizong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Xianping, Xizai was enshrined for joint sacrifice in the temple of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 熙政後至供備庫副使。

translations.literal: Xizheng later reached the post of Vice Commissioner of the Commissary Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Xizheng later rose to Vice Commissioner of the Commissary Depot.

sentences.zh: 中孚至尚書虞部員外郎，子行簡，大中祥符進士。

translations.literal: Zhongfu reached Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat; his son Xingjian passed the jinshi examination in Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat; his son Xingjian passed the jinshi examination in the Dazhong Xiangfu era.

sentences.zh: 子 中立

translations.literal: Son Zhongli
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongli

sentences.zh: 中立，字表臣，年十三而孤。

translations.literal: Zhongli, style Biaochen, was orphaned at the age of thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli, courtesy name Biaochen, lost his father at thirteen.

sentences.zh: 性疏曠，好諧謔，人不以為怒。

translations.literal: By nature he was free and easy, fond of joking and banter, and people did not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Easygoing by nature, he loved wit and banter, yet no one ever took offense.

sentences.zh: 初補西頭供奉官，後五年，改光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Western Palace Attendant; five years later he was changed to Director of the Directorate of Foodstuffs.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a Western Palace Attendant; five years later he was made Director of the Directorate of Foodstuffs.

sentences.zh: 家財悉推與諸父，無所愛。

translations.literal: He turned over all the family wealth to his uncles and kept nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all the family wealth to his uncles, keeping nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 擢直集賢院，與李宗諤、楊億、劉筠、陳越相厚善。

translations.literal: He was selected for appointment to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and was on close terms with Li Zong'e, Yang Yi, Liu Jun, and Chen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, where he formed close friendships with Li Zong'e, Yang Yi, Liu Jun, and Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 校讎秘書，凡更中立者，人皆傳之。

translations.literal: In collating secretarial texts, whenever Zhongli revised a passage, people all circulated it.
translations.idiomatic: When collating secretarial texts, any passage he revised was eagerly copied and passed around.

sentences.zh: 判三司理欠、憑由司。

translations.literal: He served concurrently as chief administrator of the Three Departments' offices for collecting arrears and managing warrants.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of the Three Departments' offices for collecting arrears and managing warrants.

sentences.zh: 帝幸亳，命修所過圖經。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Bozhou, he was ordered to compile a gazetteer of the route taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Bozhou, he was ordered to compile a gazetteer of the imperial route.

sentences.zh: 為鹽鐵判官，累遷尚書禮部侍郎，判吏部南曹。

translations.literal: He served as Salt and Iron Commissioner, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, and concurrently supervised the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Salt and Iron Commissioner, rose to Vice Minister of Rites, and supervised the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 注釋御集，為檢閱官。

translations.literal: He annotated the imperial collected works and served as proofreading official.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the imperial collected works and served as a proofreading official.

sentences.zh: 改判戶部勾院，遷戶部郎中、史館修撰，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise the Ministry of Revenue's clearing office, promoted to Director of the Revenue Bureau and History Office compiler, and charged with investigating capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervise the Ministry of Revenue's clearing office, promoted to Director of the Revenue Bureau and History Office compiler, and given charge of investigating capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 以吏部郎中、知制誥領審官院。

translations.literal: As Director of the Personnel Bureau and drafter of edicts, he also headed the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of the Personnel Bureau and drafter of edicts, he also headed the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments.

sentences.zh: 又同知禮部貢舉，判集賢院。

translations.literal: He also co-managed the Ministry of Rites examinations and concurrently directed the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He also co-managed the Ministry of Rites examinations and directed the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 坐舉官不當，落史館修撰，罷審官院。

translations.literal: Because he had recommended an official improperly, he was stripped of his title as History Office compiler and removed from the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: For improperly recommending an official, he was stripped of his History Office compiler title and removed from the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復糾察刑獄，領三班院。

translations.literal: Before long, he again investigated capital criminal cases and headed the Three Ranks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again charged with investigating capital criminal cases and given charge of the Three Ranks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 歷右諫議大夫、給事中，入為翰林學士，判秘閣。

translations.literal: He successively served as Right Remonstrance Counselor and Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, entered service as Hanlin Academician, and directed the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Right Remonstrance Counselor and Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, entered the Hanlin Academy, and directed the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 知制誥並知貢舉，詔中立與張觀兼行外制，遷尚書禮部侍郎，為學士承旨兼龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: As drafter of edicts he also managed the examinations; an edict ordered Zhongli and Zhang Guan jointly to handle external edicts. He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, made Senior Academician, and also Dragon Hall Academician.
translations.idiomatic: As drafter of edicts he also managed the examinations; the court ordered Zhongli and Zhang Guan jointly to handle external edicts. He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, made Senior Academician, and also appointed Dragon Hall Academician.

sentences.zh: 景佑四年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyou, he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingyou he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 明年，災異數見，諫官韓琦言：「中立在位，喜詼笑，非大臣體。」

translations.literal: The next year, as anomalies and portents appeared repeatedly, Remonstrance Official Han Qi said: "Zhongli in office delights in jesting and laughter — this is not the bearing of a great minister."
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as portents and anomalies appeared one after another, Remonstrance Official Han Qi said: "Zhongli in office delights in jesting and laughter — this is not the bearing of a great minister."

sentences.zh: 與王隨、陳堯佐、韓億皆罷，以戶部侍郎為資政殿學士，領通進銀臺司，判尚書都省，進大學士。

translations.literal: He was dismissed together with Wang Sui, Chen Yaozhuo, and Han Yi, and with the rank of Vice Minister of Revenue was made Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Talent, headed the Directorate for Presentation of Memorials, supervised the Secretariat Directorate, and was advanced to Grand Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed together with Wang Sui, Chen Yaozhuo, and Han Yi, and with the rank of Vice Minister of Revenue was made Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Talent, put in charge of the Directorate for Presentation of Memorials, given supervision of the Secretariat Directorate, and promoted to Grand Academician.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎、提舉祥源觀，以太子少傅致仕，遷少師。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and put in charge of the Xiangyuan Shrine; he retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and was promoted to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and put in charge of the Xiangyuan Shrine, retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and was promoted to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太傅，諡文定。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Senior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously granted Senior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Wendi.

sentences.zh: 中立練習臺閣故事，不汲汲近名。

translations.literal: Zhongli was well versed in palace and archive precedents and did not eagerly chase after a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli was thoroughly versed in palace and archive precedents and never eagerly pursued fame.

sentences.zh: 喜賓客，客至必與飲酒，醉乃得去。

translations.literal: He delighted in entertaining guests; when guests arrived he always drank with them, and only when drunk could they leave.
translations.idiomatic: He loved entertaining guests; whenever they came he insisted on drinking with them, and none could leave until he was thoroughly drunk.

sentences.zh: 初，家產歲入百萬錢，末年費幾盡。

translations.literal: At first the household's annual income was a million cash; in his later years it was nearly all spent.
translations.idiomatic: At first his household drew an annual income of a million cash; by his later years he had spent nearly all of it.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其病，賜白金三百兩。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of his illness, he granted three hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard he was ill, he granted him three hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 既死，其家至不能辦喪。

translations.literal: After his death, his family could not even manage the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his family could not even afford to arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 子居簡，至太子中允、集賢校理。

translations.literal: His son Jujian reached Vice Director of the Eastern Palace and Academy proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jujian rose to Vice Director of the Eastern Palace and proofreader in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 李穆，字孟雍，開封府陽武人。

translations.literal: Li Mu, style Mengyong, was a native of Yangwu in Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu, courtesy name Mengyong, was a native of Yangwu in Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父咸秩，陝西大都督府司馬。

translations.literal: His father Xianzhi was Military Administrator of the Great Protectorate in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianzhi served as Military Administrator of the Great Protectorate in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 穆幼能屬文，有至行。

translations.literal: From youth Mu could compose texts and possessed the utmost conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Mu could compose prose and possessed the highest moral character.

sentences.zh: 行路得遺物，必訪主歸之。

translations.literal: When walking on the road he found lost objects, he always sought out the owner and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he found something lost on the road, he always tracked down the owner and returned it.

sentences.zh: 從酸棗王昭素受《易》及《莊》、《老》書，盡究其義。

translations.literal: He studied the Book of Changes, the Zhuangzi, and the Laozi under Wang Zhaosu of Suozao, exhaustively investigating their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Book of Changes, the Zhuangzi, and the Laozi under Wang Zhaosu of Suozao, probing their meaning to the fullest.

sentences.zh: 昭素謂曰：「子所得皆精理，往往出吾意表。」

translations.literal: Wang Zhaosu said to him: "What you have attained is all refined principle, often beyond what I had expected."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhaosu told him: "Everything you have grasped is refined principle, often beyond anything I anticipated."

sentences.zh: 且語人曰：「李生異日必為廊廟器。」

translations.literal: He also told others: "This young Li will surely become a pillar of state in days to come."
translations.idiomatic: He also told others: "This young Li will surely become a pillar of the state one day."

sentences.zh: 以所著《易論》三十三篇授之。

translations.literal: He bequeathed to him his thirty-three essays on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He then bequeathed to him his thirty-three essays on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，以進士為郢、汝二州從事，遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: In early Xiande of the Later Zhou, having passed the jinshi examination he served as aide in Ying and Ru prefectures and was transferred to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xiande of the Later Zhou, after passing the jinshi examination he served as aide in Ying and Ru prefectures and was promoted to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 宋初，以殿中侍御史選為洋州通判。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, as Palace Vice Censor he was selected as Military Commissioner of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song, as Palace Vice Censor he was selected as Military Commissioner of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既至，剖決滯訟，無留獄焉。

translations.literal: After he arrived, he adjudicated backlogged lawsuits, and there were no detained cases.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he cleared the backlog of lawsuits, leaving no case undecided.

sentences.zh: 移陝州通判，有司調郡租輸河南，穆以本鎮軍食闕，不即應命，坐免。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Military Commissioner of Shaan Prefecture. When the authorities ordered county rents transported to Henan, Mu, because local military provisions were deficient, did not immediately comply with the order and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of Shaan Prefecture. When the authorities ordered county rents shipped to Henan, Mu, noting that local military provisions were short, did not comply at once and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又坐舉官，削前資。

translations.literal: He was again punished for recommending an official and stripped of his prior rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was again punished for an improper recommendation and stripped of his prior rank.

sentences.zh: 時弟肅為博州從事，穆將母就肅居，雖貧甚，兄弟相與講學，意泊如也。

translations.literal: At that time his younger brother Su was aide in Bo Prefecture; Mu moved with his mother to live with Su. Though extremely poor, the brothers studied together, their minds serene and content.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his younger brother Su was aide in Bo Prefecture; Mu moved with his mother to join Su. Though desperately poor, the brothers studied together in tranquil contentment.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，以太子中允召。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜左拾遺、知制誥。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Left Remonstrator and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Left Remonstrator and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 五代以還，詞令尚華靡，至穆而獨用雅正，悉矯其弊。

translations.literal: Since the return of the Five Dynasties, edicts had favored ornate language; Mu alone used refined correctness and entirely corrected these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, edicts had favored ornate language; Mu alone wrote in refined, correct prose and wholly corrected the abuse.

sentences.zh: 穆與盧多遜為同門生，太祖嘗謂多遜：「李穆性仁善，辭學之外無所豫。」

translations.literal: Mu and Lu Duosun had been fellow students. Taizu once said to Duosun: "Li Mu is benevolent in nature; beyond literary study he has no other concerns."
translations.idiomatic: Mu and Lu Duosun had been classmates. Taizu once said to Duosun: "Li Mu is benevolent by nature; apart from letters he has no other interests."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「穆操行端直，臨事不以生死易節，仁而有勇者也。」

translations.literal: Duosun replied: "Mu's conduct is upright; in critical affairs he does not change his integrity for life or death — a man both benevolent and courageous."
translations.idiomatic: Duosun replied: "Mu's conduct is upright; in critical affairs he will not trade his integrity for life or death — a man both benevolent and courageous."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「誠如是，吾當用之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If it is truly so, I shall employ him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If that is truly so, I shall employ him."

sentences.zh: 時將有事江南，已部分諸將，而未有發兵之端。

translations.literal: At that time action against Jiangnan was planned; the generals had already been deployed, but there was not yet a pretext for launching troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court planned action against Jiangnan; the generals had already been deployed, but no pretext for launching troops had yet been found.

sentences.zh: 乃先召李煜入朝，以穆為使。

translations.literal: So they first summoned Li Yu to court and made Mu the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore first summoned Li Yu to court and appointed Mu as envoy.

sentences.zh: 穆至諭旨，煜辭以疾，且言：「事大朝以望全濟，今若此，有死而已。」

translations.literal: When Mu arrived and conveyed the imperial message, Yu declined on grounds of illness and also said: "Serving the great court, I hoped for complete preservation; now if it comes to this, there is only death."
translations.idiomatic: When Mu arrived and delivered the imperial message, Yu declined on grounds of illness and said: "Serving the great court, I had hoped to be preserved whole; if it comes to this, I can only accept death."

sentences.zh: 穆曰：「朝與否，國主自處之。

translations.literal: Mu said: "Whether to attend court or not, the lord of the state must decide for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Mu said: "Whether to attend court is for Your Majesty to decide.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷甲兵精銳，物力雄富，恐不易當其鋒，宜熟思之，無自貽後悔。」

translations.literal: Yet the court's armor and troops are sharp and elite, its material strength abundant and rich; I fear it will not be easy to meet their edge. You should think carefully and not bring regret upon yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court's armor and troops are sharp and elite, its resources abundant and strong; I fear you will not easily withstand their edge. Think carefully, and do not bring regret upon yourself."

sentences.zh: 使還，具言狀，上以為所諭要切。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, he reported the full circumstances; the emperor considered his counsel urgent and essential.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu returned, he reported everything in full; the emperor found his counsel urgent and essential.

sentences.zh: 江南亦謂其言誠實。

translations.literal: Jiangnan also considered his words sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan, too, regarded his words as sincere.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was transferred to Left Supplementation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiping Xingguo era he was transferred to Left Supplementation Officer.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，加史館修撰、判館事，面賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he was additionally made History Office compiler and director of office affairs, and was conferred gold and purple insignia in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he was additionally made History Office compiler and director of office affairs, and received the gold-and-purple insignia in person.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征太原還，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after returning from the campaign against Taiyuan, he was appointed Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after returning from the Taiyuan campaign, he was appointed Attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 預修《太祖實錄》，賜衣帶、銀器、繒彩。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu and was granted robes, belt, silver vessels, and silk brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu and was granted robes, belt, silver vessels, and silk brocade.

sentences.zh: 七年，以與盧多遜款狎，又為秦王廷美草朝辭笏記，為言者所劾，責授司封員外郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because of intimate relations with Lu Duosun and because he had drafted Prince Qin's court farewell memorial for receiving the audience tablet, he was impeached by critics and demoted to Vice Director of the Seals Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, for his close relations with Lu Duosun and for drafting Prince Qin's court farewell memorial, he was impeached by critics and demoted to Vice Director of the Seals Bureau.

sentences.zh: 八年春，與宋白等同知貢舉，及侍上御崇政殿親試進士，上憫其顏貌臒瘁，即日復拜中書舍人、史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, together with Song Bai and others he co-managed the examinations, and when attending the emperor as he personally examined jinshi candidates in Chongzheng Hall, the emperor, pitying his haggard appearance, that same day restored him as Attendant of the Central Secretariat, History Office compiler, and director of office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year, as he co-managed the examinations with Song Bai and others and attended the emperor's personal jinshi examination in Chongzheng Hall, the emperor, pitying his haggard appearance, that same day restored him as Attendant of the Central Secretariat, History Office compiler, and director of office affairs.

sentences.zh: 五月，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 六月，知開封府，剖判精敏，奸猾無所假貸，由是豪右屏跡，權貴無敢干以私，上益知其才。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was made Prefect of Kaifeng; his adjudications were sharp and keen, and the cunning were given no leniency. Hence the powerful families retreated from sight, and the nobles dared not interfere on private grounds; the emperor increasingly recognized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made Prefect of Kaifeng. His judgments were sharp and keen, and the cunning found no quarter; powerful families vanished from sight, and the nobility dared not interfere for private ends. The emperor came to know his talent ever more fully.

sentences.zh: 十一月，擢拜左諫議大夫、參知政事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was promoted and appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor and Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Counselor and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 月餘，丁母憂，未幾，起復本官。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he entered mourning for his mother; before long he was recalled to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he entered mourning for his mother; before long he was recalled to his original post.

sentences.zh: 穆三上表乞終制，詔強起之，穆益哀毀盡禮。

translations.literal: Mu three times submitted memorials begging to complete the mourning observances; an edict forcibly recalled him, yet Mu grieved ever more deeply and observed the rites with utmost devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Mu three times memorialized begging to complete his mourning; an edict forcibly recalled him, yet he grieved ever more deeply and observed every rite with utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，晨起將朝，風眩暴卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, as he rose in the morning to attend court, he suffered sudden dizziness and died abruptly at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year, as he rose to attend court in the morning, he suffered a sudden dizzy collapse and died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 穆自責授員外郎，復中書舍人，入翰林，參知政事，以至於卒，不及周歲。

translations.literal: From the time he was demoted to Vice Director, restored as Attendant of the Central Secretariat, entered the Hanlin Academy, and became Vice Grand Councilor until his death, not even one full year had passed.
translations.idiomatic: From his demotion to Vice Director through restoration as Attendant of the Central Secretariat, entry into the Hanlin Academy, and appointment as Vice Grand Councilor until his death, less than a full year had passed.

sentences.zh: 上聞其死，哭謂近臣曰：「穆國之良臣，朕方倚用，遽茲淪沒，非斯人之不幸，乃朕之不幸也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of his death, he wept and said to close ministers: "Mu was a fine minister of the state; I was just about to rely on him, when suddenly he fell and perished. This is not that man's misfortune — it is my misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of his death, he wept and told his close ministers: "Mu was a fine minister of the state; I was just about to rely on him when he suddenly fell and perished. This is not his misfortune — it is mine."

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 穆性至孝，母嘗臥疾，每動止轉側，皆親自扶掖，乃稱母意。

translations.literal: Mu's nature was the utmost in filial piety. When his mother lay ill, with every movement and turning in bed he personally supported her until it satisfied his mother's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was utterly filial by nature. When his mother lay ill, he personally supported her at every movement and turn in bed until she was content.

sentences.zh: 初，穆坐秦王事屬吏，其子惟簡紿祖母以穆奉詔鞫獄臺中。

translations.literal: At first, when Mu was implicated in Prince Qin's affair by subordinate officials, his son Weijian deceived his grandmother, saying that Mu had been ordered to investigate a case in the prison office.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu was first implicated in Prince Qin's affair by subordinate officials, his son Weijian deceived his grandmother, telling her that Mu had been ordered to investigate a case at the prison office.

sentences.zh: 及責授為省郎，還家，亦不以白母。

translations.literal: When he was demoted to a provincial official and returned home, he also did not tell his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he was demoted to a provincial official and returned home, he still did not tell his mother.

sentences.zh: 每隔日，陽為入直，即訪親友，或遊僧寺。

translations.literal: Every other day he pretended to enter regular duty, but in fact visited friends and relatives or wandered in Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: Every other day he pretended to report for regular duty while in fact visiting friends and relatives or wandering Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 免歸，暨於牽復，母終弗之知。

translations.literal: From dismissal through recall and restoration to office, his mother never knew.
translations.idiomatic: From dismissal through recall and restoration to office, his mother never knew.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，思慕以至滅性。

translations.literal: When in mourning, his yearning grief reached the point of damaging his health.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning, his grief was so consuming that it nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 穆善篆隸，又工畫，常晦其事。

translations.literal: Mu was skilled in seal and clerical script and also adept at painting, but he usually concealed these pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was skilled in seal and clerical script and also adept at painting, yet he usually kept these talents hidden.

sentences.zh: 質厚忠恪，謹言慎行，所為純至，無有矯飾。

translations.literal: Sincere, thick, loyal, and devoted, cautious in speech and careful in conduct, his actions were purely sincere, without any affected ornamentation.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere, steadfast, loyal, and devoted, cautious in speech and careful in action, his conduct was utterly genuine, without a trace of affectation.

sentences.zh: 深信釋典，善談名理，接引後進，多所薦達。

translations.literal: He deeply believed the Buddhist scriptures, was adept at discussing Buddhist principles, guided and supported juniors, and many he recommended and elevated.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply believed the Buddhist scriptures, was adept at discussing Buddhist principles, guided younger men, and recommended many to advancement.

sentences.zh: 尤寬厚，家人未嘗見其喜慍。

translations.literal: He was especially generous and magnanimous; family members never saw him show joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially generous and magnanimous; his family never once saw him show joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 所著文章，隨即毀之，多不留稿。

translations.literal: The compositions he wrote he immediately destroyed; most drafts were not kept.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed his written compositions as soon as they were finished; he kept almost no drafts.

sentences.zh: 子 惟簡

translations.literal: Son Weijian
translations.idiomatic: His son Weijian

sentences.zh: 子惟簡，以父任將作監丞，多才藝，性冲澹，不樂仕進。

translations.literal: Weijian, through his father's office, was appointed Director of the Directorate of Imperial Construction; he was multitalented, by nature calm and detached, and did not delight in pursuing office.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian, appointed through his father's office as Director of the Directorate of Imperial Construction, was multitalented, calm and detached by nature, and took no pleasure in official advancement.

sentences.zh: 去官家居三十餘年，人多稱之。

translations.literal: Leaving office, he lived at home for more than thirty years, and many people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he lived at home for more than thirty years, and many people praised him.

sentences.zh: 真宗素聞其有履行，景德三年，詔授惟簡子郯將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong had long heard of his conduct; in the third year of Jingde an edict granted Weijian's son Tan the post of Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong had long heard of his integrity; in the third year of Jingde an edict granted Weijian's son Tan the post of Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Construction.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年冬，召惟簡入對，特拜太子中允致仕，後加太常丞。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Weijian was summoned for audience and was specially appointed Vice Director of the Eastern Palace with retirement; later he was additionally made Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Weijian was summoned for audience and was specially appointed Vice Director of the Eastern Palace with retirement; later he was additionally made Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，卒，賜其家錢十萬，仍給郯月奉終制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi he died; the court granted his family one hundred thousand cash and continued Tan's monthly salary until the mourning period was complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxi he died; the court granted his family one hundred thousand cash and continued Tan's monthly salary until mourning was complete.

sentences.zh: 郯後為太子中舍。

translations.literal: Tan later became Vice Director of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tan later rose to Vice Director of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 弟 肅

translations.literal: Younger brother Su
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Su

sentences.zh: 肅，字季雍，七歲誦書知大義，十歲為詩，往往有警語。

translations.literal: Su, style Jiyong, at seven recited the classics and understood their great principles; at ten he composed poetry, often with striking phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Su, courtesy name Jiyong, at seven could recite the classics and grasp their meaning; at ten he wrote poetry, often with striking lines.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，登甲科。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and attained the top category.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top category.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒。

translations.literal: By nature he was fond of wine.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was fond of wine.

sentences.zh: 歷濮、博二州從事，遷保靜軍節度推官。

translations.literal: He successively served as aide in Pu and Bo prefectures and was transferred to military commissioner aide at Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as aide in Pu and Bo prefectures and was transferred to military commissioner aide at Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 詔方下，一夕與親友會飲，酣寢而卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: The edict had just been issued when one evening, feasting with friends and relatives, he fell into drunken sleep and died at the age of thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had just been issued when one evening, after feasting with friends and relatives, he fell into drunken sleep and died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《大宋樂章》九首，取九成、九夏之義，以頌國家盛德，其文甚工。

translations.literal: He once composed Great Song Hymns in nine pieces, taking the meaning of the Nine Accomplishments and Nine Summer rituals to praise the state's flourishing virtue; the writing was very refined.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed Great Song Hymns in nine pieces, invoking the Nine Accomplishments and Nine Summer rituals to praise the state's flourishing virtue; the writing was very fine.

sentences.zh: 又作《代周顒答北山移文》、《吊幽憂子文》、《病雞賦》，意皆有所規焉。

translations.literal: He also composed Reply to Zhou Yong on Behalf of Bei Mountain, Elegy for You-you-zi, and Lament for the Ailing Cock; in each the intent was to offer admonition.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Reply to Zhou Yong on Behalf of Bei Mountain, Elegy for You-you-zi, and Lament for the Ailing Cock — each intended as a work of admonition.

sentences.zh: 論曰：張昭居五季之末，專以典章撰述為事，博洽文史，旁通治亂，君違必諫，時君雖嘉尚之而不能從。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Zhang Zhao, at the end of the Five Dynasties, devoted himself solely to drafting institutions and composing texts; widely versed in literature and history, he also comprehended governance and disorder. Whenever the ruler went astray he remonstrated, yet though the rulers of the time praised and honored him, they could not follow his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: At the end of the Five Dynasties, Zhang Zhao devoted himself solely to drafting institutions and composing texts. Widely versed in literature and history and thoroughly acquainted with governance and disorder, he remonstrated whenever a ruler went astray; yet though the rulers of his day praised and honored him, they could not follow his counsel.

sentences.zh: 宋興，敦獎碩儒，多所詢訪，庶幾獲稽古之效矣。

translations.literal: When the Song rose, it earnestly rewarded great scholars and extensively consulted them, almost obtaining the effect of examining antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song rose, it earnestly rewarded great scholars and consulted them widely, almost achieving the effect of grounding policy in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 竇氏弟昆以儒學進，並馳時望。

translations.literal: The Dou brothers Yi and Kun advanced through Confucian learning and jointly rode the renown of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou brothers Yi and Kun rose through Confucian learning and together enjoyed the renown of the age.

sentences.zh: 儀之剛方清介，有應務之才，將試大用而遽淪亡。

translations.literal: Yi was firm, upright, and incorruptible, with talent for handling practical affairs; he was about to be greatly employed when he suddenly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was firm, upright, and incorruptible, with a talent for practical affairs; he was on the verge of great appointment when he suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 儼優遊文藝，修起禮樂。

translations.literal: Yan was leisurely in literary arts and restored rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: Yan moved gracefully through literary pursuits and helped restore rites and music.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京，偁實元僚，冲淡回翔，晚著忠讜。

translations.literal: When Taizong governed the capital, he called him a true original aide; calmly circling through office, in his later years he manifested loyal candor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong governed the capital, he called Yan a true original aide; moving calmly through office, in his later years he showed loyal candor.

sentences.zh: 若其門族宦業之盛，世或以為陰德之報，其亦義方之效也。

translations.literal: As for the flourishing of their clan's official achievements, the world sometimes regarded it as repayment of hidden virtue — also the effect of righteous family teaching.
translations.idiomatic: As for the flourishing official careers of their clan, the world sometimes took it as repayment of hidden virtue — the fruit, too, of righteous family teaching.

sentences.zh: 餘慶當太祖居潛，歷任幕府，名亞趙普、李處耘；

translations.literal: Yuqing, when Taizu was still in concealment, successively served in staff offices; his name stood below Zhao Pu and Li Chuyun.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was still in concealment, Yuqing served successively in staff offices, his standing below Zhao Pu and Li Chuyun.

sentences.zh: 及二人登用，一不介意，其後相繼為眾所傾，乃能為之辯釋。

translations.literal: When the two were employed, he did not mind at all; afterward, when they were successively toppled by the masses, he was able to offer defense and explanation for them.
translations.idiomatic: When the two were elevated to power he did not mind at all; later, when they were successively brought down by public opinion, he was able to speak in their defense.

sentences.zh: 熙古居大任，自處如寒素。

translations.literal: Xigu held great responsibility yet conducted himself like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Xigu bore great responsibility yet lived as simply as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 熙載立朝，言無顧避，喜薦善人。

translations.literal: Xizai in court spoke without looking back and delighted in recommending good men.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai spoke in court without hesitation and delighted in recommending worthy men.

sentences.zh: 穆以文學孝行見稱於時。

translations.literal: Mu was praised in his time for literary learning and filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was praised in his time for his literary learning and filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 數賢雖當創業之始，而進退之際，藹然承平多士之風焉，宜宋治之日進於盛也。

translations.literal: These several worthies, though they lived at the founding's beginning, in their advancement and retreat manifested the serene manner of the many scholars of a peaceful age; it was fitting that Song governance daily advanced toward flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: These worthy men, though they lived at the dynasty's founding, carried themselves in advancement and retreat with the serene grace of scholars in a peaceful age — fitting harbingers of a Song order that daily grew toward greatness.
